title: Tax Preparer Accused of Claiming Losses on Crypto Never Owned
summary: A Connecticut tax preparer allegedly claimed cryptocurrency losses for taxpayers who never owned the assets. The accusations form part of a broader federal prosecution involving fabricated deductions and the alleged diversion of refunds. Prosecutors Allege Crypto Losses on Nonexistent Holdings Losse...
content:
A Connecticut tax preparer allegedly claimed cryptocurrency losses for taxpayers who never owned the assets. The accusations form part of a broader federal prosecution involving fabricated deductions and the alleged diversion of refunds.

Key Takeaways

  • Yuridia Trujillo faces 19 counts involving false income tax returns.
  • Alleged crypto losses involved assets taxpayers never owned.
  • Portions of refunds allegedly flowed into the preparer’s and an associate’s accounts.

Prosecutors Allege Crypto Losses on Nonexistent Holdings

Losses on cryptocurrency that taxpayers never owned allegedly appeared on returns prepared by Yuridia Trujillo of Meriden, Connecticut, authorities announced on Oct. 22. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) detailed the alleged false-return scheme involving her business, Yuri’s LLC. She prepared at least 4,335 returns for tax years 2017 through 2024.

According to the indictment, many filings contained false entries involving retirement contributions, dependent care, businesses, and rental properties. The announcement described:

“… fictitious losses for the buying and selling of stocks and cryptocurrency that clients never owned”

Trujillo also allegedly used Form 8888, which allows taxpayers to split a direct-deposit refund among up to three bank accounts, to direct portions of taxpayers’ refunds into bank accounts belonging to herself and an associate.

A federal grand jury returned the indictment Oct. 7, and authorities arrested her Oct. 9. She is released on a $50,000 bond pending trial. Each charge of aiding and assisting in the preparation and presentation of a false income tax return carries up to three years in prison upon conviction. The charges remain allegations, and she is presumed innocent unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

How Investment Losses Can Reduce Taxable Income

Legitimate losses on cryptocurrency held for investment can offset capital gains under the rules governing U.S. cryptocurrency taxation. A capital loss generally arises when an investment sells for less than its adjusted basis, usually its purchase cost with applicable adjustments.

When capital losses exceed gains, taxpayers can generally deduct up to $3,000 of the difference against other income, or $1,500 if married filing separately. The IRS’s capital loss deduction limits also permit unused amounts to carry forward into later years.

Transaction records substantiate the amounts reported, including receipts, sales, exchanges, and the dollar value of cryptocurrency at the relevant time. Established crypto transaction reporting requirements include using Form 8949, which lists individual asset sales and exchanges, to calculate most investment gains and losses, then summarizing them on Schedule D, the section of a federal return that totals capital gains and deductible losses.

False Cost Figures and Expanded Broker Reporting

Misstating an investment’s purchase cost can also reduce reported gains, as demonstrated by Frank Richard Ahlgren III’s guilty plea in a separate Texas case. The Austin bitcoin investor inflated the cost basis of bitcoin sold in 2017.

Ahlgren subsequently received a two-year sentence for false crypto tax reporting on Dec. 12, 2024, the Justice Department announced. The court also ordered $1,095,031 in restitution to the United States.

Federal reporting rules now provide the IRS with more information about covered transactions through digital asset broker reporting requirements finalized in 2024. Brokers report gross proceeds, or sale amounts before subtracting costs, for 2025 transactions in 2026. Reporting of purchase-cost information for certain 2026 transactions follows in 2027.

title: A16z Frontier Broadens The Pitch For Crypto As Investors Look Across Technologies
summary: Andreessen Horowitz is expanding its crypto team's investment brief. Chris Dixon's October 22 announcement renames a16z Crypto as a16z Frontier, with the new fund able to pursue a wider range of emerging technologies while continuing crypto investment.
content:
Andreessen Horowitz is expanding its crypto team’s investment brief. Chris Dixon’s October 22 announcement renames a16z Crypto as a16z Frontier, with the new fund able to pursue a wider range of emerging technologies while continuing crypto investment.

TL;DR

  • A broader mandate changes the set of businesses considered for funding.
  • Using a blockchain does not determine a company’s customers or revenue model.
  • Commercial demand remains the test for products combining AI and crypto.

The business model becomes more useful than the sector label

The announcement is a change in investment scope. It does not establish how much of future spending will reach any particular technology.

For a founder, the practical question is which problem a prospective investor understands. A payments company using stablecoins may need distribution, banking access and regulatory expertise. A data marketplace may need rights management and reliable buyers. Calling both crypto companies does little to identify the skills that will make either successful.

That difference is already visible in products available today. Circle’s institutional funding documentation deals with reserved balances, settlement and withdrawal routes. These are treasury operations, even though USDC is involved throughout the process.

Similarly, USD.AI distinguishes a governance instrument from the instrument receiving lending income. A project can use tokens at several layers while its underlying commercial task remains financing computing equipment.

The distinction helps explain the variety in BitGo’s move into consumer applications. Infrastructure expertise may support a new product, but it does not eliminate the separate work of attracting users and keeping them engaged.

Combining AI and crypto still needs a paying customer

A broader investment mandate can accommodate companies whose activity does not fit an existing sector neatly. That is useful when a product relies on several technologies at once. It also makes comparison more demanding: a hardware business, a financial intermediary and a software service cannot be evaluated with the same measures.

For a hypothetical AI service purchasing data automatically, blockchain payments might solve a transaction problem. They would not settle whether the purchased data improves the service, whether its use is licensed or whether customers will pay enough to cover the cost.

Those remaining questions determine the business. Faster settlement can improve working capital without creating demand. Automated spending can remove a manual task while also making spending limits and authorization more important.

Payment-fraud screening is one example of the controls that have to accompany easier transfers. And actual payment usage offers more evidence of utility than attaching a new label to a balance sheet.

The rebranding creates room for more kinds of company to enter the investment conversation. Its eventual significance for crypto will depend on the businesses funded, the products they deliver and whether users need the blockchain functions those products contain.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: California Opposes SEC Crypto Plan Over Investor Protection Risks
summary: California is challenging an SEC crypto proposal that state officials warn could weaken investor protections by limiting their review of offerings. The dispute centers on federal fundraising exemptions and states’ ability to screen investments before sales. California Warns of Weaker Investment Scre...
content:
California is challenging an SEC crypto proposal that state officials warn could weaken investor protections by limiting their review of offerings. The dispute centers on federal fundraising exemptions and states’ ability to screen investments before sales.

Key Takeaways

  • DFPI opposed the SEC proposal in a comment letter to the agency.
  • Proposed exemptions would permit qualifying raises up to $75 million.
  • States would retain authority to investigate securities fraud.

California Warns of Weaker Investment Screening

Investors could lose a layer of protection against risky crypto offerings under a federal proposal, California’s financial regulator warned on Oct. 21. The Department of Financial Protection and Innovation (DFPI) outlined its opposition to Regulation Crypto Assets after submitting a comment letter to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

DFPI Commissioner KC Mohseni stated:

“California champions innovation and the entrepreneurs who drive it. What we will not accept is a coordinated attempt by federal regulators to override state authority and protections while stepping back from the oversight they are supposed to provide.”

Federal securities law preserves states’ authority to investigate fraud, deceit, and unlawful broker or dealer conduct. California’s objection focuses on losing preventive screening tools through federal limits on state registration and qualification requirements.

SEC Sets Offering Limits and Disclosure Duties

Qualifying issuers could raise up to $5 million over four years through a startup exemption, while a separate crypto fundraising exemption would permit up to $75 million per 12-month period.

Both routes would require narrative disclosures: written explanations of the project, its risks, and other information investors need to evaluate an offering. The SEC’s proposed crypto offering framework would also require financial statements and ongoing reporting under the fundraising route. Federal antifraud provisions would continue to apply.

Chairman Paul Atkins has presented tailored crypto exemptions as a way to bring issuers and capital formation to the United States. An investment contract generally involves investing in a common enterprise with expected profits derived from others’ managerial efforts.

A conditional safe harbor would allow a crypto asset to cease being subject to an investment contract when specified legal conditions are met. These include completing or permanently ending promised essential managerial efforts, the work investors rely on to generate expected profits.

Industry Support Contrasts With State Fraud Concerns

Industry support includes blockchain payments company Ripple, crypto exchange Coinbase (Nasdaq: COIN), and exchange operator Nasdaq (Nasdaq: NDAQ), each seeking changes to the SEC proposal. Ripple requests trading safeguards, while Coinbase seeks clearer rules for subsequent token sales. Nasdaq emphasizes preserving investor protections for traditional securities, including tokenized stocks and funds.

State officials cite continuing exposure to crypto investment fraud schemes as grounds for preserving oversight. DFPI reported adding nearly 200 crypto-related scams to its tracker, a 30% increase from the previous year.

Officials also warn the proposed approach could extend beyond digital assets to other investment products. California plans to examine other longstanding laws it could use to address market manipulation and deceit.

title: Standard Chartered-led Anchorpoint says it’s not rushing retail stablecoin
summary: The Standard Chartered and Animoca Brands joint venture previously targeted retail access as early as the end of 2026, but its CEO declined to reaffirm that timeline.
content:
The Standard Chartered and Animoca Brands joint venture previously targeted retail access as early as the end of 2026, but its CEO declined to reaffirm that timeline.

Standard Chartered-backed stablecoin venture Anchorpoint says it will take a cautious approach to opening its Hong Kong dollar-backed stablecoin to retail users, declining to confirm a launch date after rival HSBC rolled out RedCoin, according to the South China Morning Post.

The venture released its institutional stablecoin product in August and previously indicated a retail offering could arrive as early as the end of 2026.

Anchorpoint CEO Dominic Maffei declined to confirm that timeline at a Friday press conference, saying the company would take a prudent approach.

“We believe it’s important to build the market out in a long-term, sustainable manner,” Maffei said, adding that rushing a launch “does not make sense.”

The update comes after HSBC launched its Hong Kong dollar-backed RedCoin on Friday for the 3.3 million users of its PayMe app.

Anchorpoint grew out of a partnership between Standard Chartered, Animoca Brands and telecommunications provider HKT, which was announced in February 2025, following their joint participation in Hong Kong’s stablecoin issuer sandbox in July 2024.

Animoca’s role is to bring its blockchain expertise and industry network to the venture and help develop uses for the stablecoin across the Web3 ecosystem.

title: Robinhood Sets A 2027 Middle East Launch Target After DFSA Authorization
summary: Robinhood announced DFSA authorization and a Dubai International Financial Centre headquarters on October 22, with a Middle East rollout planned for 2027. Regulatory permission precedes customer availability.
content:
Robinhood announced DFSA authorization and a Dubai International Financial Centre headquarters on October 22, with a Middle East rollout planned for 2027. Regulatory permission precedes customer availability.

TL;DR

  • The announcement concerns a planned regional rollout.
  • Permissions, product terms and local funding arrangements will shape actual access.
  • Crypto, shares and investment tokens can carry different rights within one app.

A financial-center authorization has a defined scope

Robinhood’s statement covers trading and custody. Those are separate functions, with different responsibilities for handling customer orders and safeguarding assets.

The regulator’s own crypto framework explains that financial-services activities involving crypto tokens in or from DIFC require appropriate authorization. It also distinguishes the use of a token from the regulated service performed with it. That distinction is relevant when a platform combines dealing, custody and access to several kinds of asset.

A regional headquarters is a base from which to build a business. It does not, by itself, establish that every product will be available to every resident of every nearby country. Customer eligibility depends on the permissions and terms governing the particular offering.

Those boundaries can be easy to miss in an app with a unified interface. Two products may sit next to each other on a screen while using different custodians, settlement processes or contractual protections.

Stock-linked perpetual contracts illustrate the importance of checking the instrument. Exposure to a share price does not necessarily mean owning the share or receiving the rights of its shareholder.

The launch will need usable banking and custody connections

Authorization creates the possibility of service; the customer experience depends on execution. Deposits, currency conversion, withdrawals, support and account recovery all become part of whether a platform is practical for ordinary users.

A low headline trading commission, for example, cannot describe the complete cost of funding an account in one currency and buying an asset quoted in another. The exchange rate, transfer method and timing can change the amount that reaches the market.

For crypto, custody arrangements add another decision. A balance recorded by a platform and assets held in a personal wallet expose users to different operational responsibilities. NewsBTC’s examination of institutional key-control structures shows why custody needs more explanation than a generic security claim.

The DFSA’s implementation guidance also identifies token-suitability assessment and continuing monitoring as regulatory concerns. Permission to operate a business is not an assurance about the future price of every asset it offers.

As with the expansion of tokenized equities, the useful next evidence will be the actual product documentation and working service. Robinhood has supplied a timetable and an authorization milestone; the rollout will determine how those translate into access.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Bank of Israel Rejects Netanyahu’s Crypto Sanction-Evasion Plan
summary: The institution stressed that instead of seeking alternatives to bypass possible international sanctions against the nation, Israel should focus on preventing these from happening and affecting the country’s economy. Netanyahu said there were other alternatives to crypto to achieve the same objectiv...
content:
The institution stressed that instead of seeking alternatives to bypass possible international sanctions against the nation, Israel should focus on preventing these from happening and affecting the country’s economy. Netanyahu said there were other alternatives to crypto to achieve the same objective.

Key Takeaways

  • PM Netanyahu proposed using cryptocurrency to bypass potential international economic sanctions.
  • The Bank of Israel opposed the idea, urging leaders to focus on preventing sanctions to protect trade.
  • Political rivals warned the crypto pivot threatens national security and could cripple tech investments.

Bank of Israel Rejects Netanyahu’s Proposal To Use Crypto To Skirt Sanctions

The Bank of Israel responded to a public proposal from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who floated the idea of using cryptocurrency to skirt hypothetical sanctions on the Israeli economy.

In a statement, the institution declared that the right thing for Israel’s economy “is preserving the economic relationships with our principal trade partners and focusing on preventing sanctions and their negative influence on the economy.” Furthermore, the bank assessed that the issue fell “within the responsibilities of the political echelon, and it should act to advance it.”

On Friday, during an interview, Netanyahu said that cryptocurrency might serve as an alternative economic path if Israel is subjected to international economic and banking sanctions derived from the nation’s military deployments.

“We need to understand that there could be banking sanctions. You need to prepare an alternative economic system, and you know what that is, and you know which currencies can bypass this, and I’m working on that as well,” Netanyahu said, pointing to crypto and blockchain technology as tools that can be leveraged to bypass these sanctions.

Netanyahu has been aware of bitcoin and cryptocurrency for a long time. In 2017, the Prime Minister stressed that banks were destined to disappear when asked if individuals should invest in bitcoin.

Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu’s main challenger in the upcoming elections, blasted the Prime Minister’s proposal, labeling it as a threat to national security. “After dismantling Israeli society and weakening the IDF, Netanyahu has set his sights on his next target: the long-term destruction of the Israeli economy for generations to come,” he declared.

“How could an Israeli high-tech company with overseas clients receive payments or secure foreign investment? How could Google acquire an Israeli firm if the condition were to bypass international banking systems and pay in cryptocurrency?” Eisenkot concluded.

Netanyahu acknowledged the Bank of Israel’s criticism and acknowledged that besides crypto, other tools were available to achieve the same goal and maintain connection to the global financial system if Israel gets targeted by international sanctions.

“I thank the Bank of Israel for their advice, but I do what I think is right-and my long-term track record shows that I have led the State of Israel to unprecedented economic prosperity,” Netanyahu declared in a recent interview.

title: Circle Match Gives USDC Desks A New Fee Trade-Off And A Separate Funding Balance
summary: Circle's October 22 update on Match describes a service for connecting institutional USDC flows. A consequential detail sits in its funding documentation: money prepared for a mint-side order remains separate from the ordinary Circle Mint wallet.
content:
Circle’s October 22 update on Match describes a service for connecting institutional USDC flows. A consequential detail sits in its funding documentation: money prepared for a mint-side order remains separate from the ordinary Circle Mint wallet.

TL;DR

  • Matched minting orders can receive the fee paid by matched redemptions.
  • The mint-side prefunding balance has a restricted exit route.
  • Execution records matter more than a headline rebate when measuring the service.

Prefunding changes what available money means

The company’s explanation connects the service to institutions with opposing liquidity needs. For a participant, the practical distinction is between making funds available for execution and actually completing the intended transaction.

Circle’s funding documentation explains an important asymmetry. A redeemer reserves USDC already held in a standard Mint wallet. On the minting side, a settled dollar wire becomes restricted Match-only USDC. That balance cannot simply be sent to a blockchain address.

If a mint-side order fills, the institution receives normal USDC in its Mint wallet. If it wants to leave with an unused restricted balance, the documented route is redemption back to dollars by wire. Canceling an order therefore does not necessarily create immediately deployable on-chain money.

For a treasury desk, the implication is an opportunity-cost calculation. Capital committed to an auction cannot simultaneously meet another payment. The relevant comparison includes the expected rebate, the chance of execution and the operational value of retaining unrestricted liquidity.

This is a different problem from the payment-volume growth discussed in NewsBTC’s stablecoin activity coverage. A widely used token can still involve distinct funding constraints at individual service providers.

The useful performance measure is the completed round trip

A successful implementation needs to reconcile what was ordered, what filled, what remained reserved and what eventually settled. An interface balance can be convenient for monitoring without being a substitute for the underlying transaction records.

The order API exposes execution information and links between rolled orders. Those records let a desk distinguish one instruction that waited through several auctions from several independent completed transactions.

That distinction matters when calculating results. Counting submitted volume would exaggerate activity if the same amount repeatedly rolls forward. Comparing the quoted fee with the realized fee alone would also ignore time spent waiting and any required fallback.

Other institutional designs, including USDC-based derivatives clearing, likewise depend on how balances become available at the moment an obligation falls due.

Payment screening remains a separate control. The checks described in Mastercard’s stablecoin-security initiative concern the transfer’s legitimacy, whereas matching concerns liquidity and execution.

Match can make opposing institutional flows economically useful to one another. The operational test is whether that benefit survives the full journey from prefunding through matching to usable money at the destination.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: AI agents help rescue ETH’s Glamsterdam fork, ‘Steal My Bitcoin’ site: Hodler’s Digest
summary: Similar to the Hugging Face hack, Ethereum researchers have set up an AI Agent message board to help rescue the Glamsterdam fork. ‘Steal My Bitcoin’ site successfully hacked.
content:
AI agents message board set up to rescue Glamsterdam fork

The second and final testnet for Ethereum’s Glamsterdam hard fork was cancelled this week, after ChainSecurity found vulnerabilities in two gas scaling Ethereum Improvement Proposals that could have spelled big trouble for at least 13 DeFi contracts.

The bugs were connected to EIP-8037/8038 and resulted in contracts, that rely on the way gas currently behaves, breaking when a call runs out of gas. It’s all fairly technical and complicated, but the upshot is that an attacker may have been able to exploit the resulting vulnerabilities.

The hard fork testnet dress rehearsal on Hoodi is not expected to be rescheduled until all the second order effects of the fork have been gamed out properly. In an article on X today, Derek Chiang from Ethlabs noted the issues were found very late in the process, which is less than ideal, “causing everyone to scramble to deal with the fallout.”

“In the future, protocol designers would do well to conduct much more thorough analysis of potential breakages that their update might introduce, and to do so much earlier in the process.”

Chiang says two researchers from Ethlabs and the Ethereum Foundation had independently spun up a bunch of AI Agents to scan contracts for vulnerabilities. When they realized they were both employing the same strategy they “set up a message board for their agents in the form of a github repo” to coordinate the work.

He noted the similarities to the OpenAI <> Hugging Face hack where rogue agents had set up a message board to coordinate the attacks. “Well, turns out the same pattern is useful for the good agents too,” he said. The exercise has been so successful at finding potential problems that a second board has been set up to examine the effects of EIP-8198, aka “Quick Slots”, which has been proposed for the subsequent Hegota hard fork.

Steal My Bitcoin site is successfully hacked

Updated October 26 12.10am UTC with the result of the challenge.

A new website that hasn’t been patched for the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities offered a Bitcoin prize in a challenge related to the biggest cybersecurity scare of the year. The ‘Steal My Bitcoin’ site hid the key to a Bitcoin wallet worth around $2000, which was accessible to the PHP user account through a binary called print-flag.

Source: StealMyBitcoin

The site generated a huge amount of interest and went offline periodically offline due to heavy traffic and probing attempts.

It was solved by KillerBoi who successfully extracted the private key — however in a plot twist, it turned out not to be the key for the wallet address shown on the site. The organizer James Pavur acknowledged this was a mistake and said the funds would be transferred.

WordFence founder Mark Maunder said the despite the key being extracted within a day: “This is the absolute best explanation you’ll see on how hard #php2shell is to exploit. The author had to trigger a precise memory corruption condition, leak internal memory addresses, bypass aslr, reverse engineer php’s internal memory structures, forge structures to hijack execution, and account for php build differences, worker behavior and timing.”

PHP is a programming language widely used to power websites and web applications, including content management systems. Government agencies and other organizations in the Netherlands, Australia, Japan, Finland and elsewhere took critical websites offline Wednesday as a precaution while emergency patches were developed for two related critical vulnerabilities. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers without logging in.

Solana’s Alpenglow launches on mainnet

Solana’s first major consensus upgrade, Alpenglow, went live on mainnet around 1:54 pm UTC on Wednesday, according to the Solana Foundation’s Alpenglow dashboard.

Agave developer Anza said the time it takes a transaction to become final has now fallen from about 12.8 seconds to roughly 150 milliseconds. In the wake of the upgrade DeFi activity has been flat or fallen slightly — but it’s early days yet.

The upgrade’s first phase, Votor, replaces the existing voting and finalization mechanism with direct validator voting and a certificate-based system, which is expected to result in the headline transaction count falling by around 60%. A later phase will introduce Rotor, a new block data-distribution protocol intended to replace Turbine.

Starknet votes to start work on becoming a post-quantum L1

Starknet’s community has voted to support research into becoming an independent, post-quantum layer-1 blockchain.

A governance vote that ran for seven days drew about 3,200 votes, with 93.52% of voting power in favor of the transition.

The actual shift itself would require a separate, binding governance vote. For now, Starknet will continue operating as an Ethereum layer-2 network. 

“We’re beginning work on a whitepaper even before we start the weekend, and hope to release a draft for public scrutiny in November,” StarkWare CEO Eli Ben-Sasson told Cointelegraph. Starknet saw the biggest fall of the top 100 coins this week, erasing one quarter of its value.

Source: Cointelegraph

US senator probes Tether after reported deal with ex-Trump crypto adviser

Senator Richard Blumenthal — the top Democrat on the Senate’s investigations subcommittee — has requested information from Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino after the Wall Street Journal reported the stablecoin firm had inked a $6.3 million deal with a marketing company co-founded by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines.

In a Thursday letter to Ardoino, the Connecticut lawmaker said that the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations demanded “records and information related to contracts, payments, communications, and lobbying” about the deal. The politician believes it may contravene rules around ethics, corruption and lobbying. Tether says an external investigation “found no evidence of wrongdoing.”

Winners and Losers

At the end of the week, Bitcoin (BTC) is down 1.2% to trade at $80,549, Ethereum (ETH) is down 1.9% to trade at $2,343 and XRP (XRP) is up 0.9% to $1.20. The total market cap is at $2.68 trillion according to CoinMarketCap.

Among the biggest 100 cryptocurrencies, the top three altcoin winners of the week are MemeCore (M) with a 24.4% gain, Venice Token (VVV) on 14.8%, and Ethena (ENA) on 14.1%.

The top three altcoin losers of the week are Starknet (STRK) which was down 24.9%, Aerodrome Finance (AERO) down 12.5% and Sei (SEI) down 12.5%.

Bitcoin weekly chart. Source: CoinMarketCap

Prediction of the Week

JPMorgan projects Bitcoin to outperform US stocks and gold over next decade

JPMorgan Asset Management projects Bitcoin (BTC) will outperform stocks and gold over the next decade, but cautions that its volatility makes it unsuitable for diversifying portfolios for now.

On Monday, JPMorgan published its 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report, projecting a 10% annualized return for Bitcoin, compared with 7.5% for large-cap US stocks and 5.5% for gold.

“At the moment, we do not make a case for Bitcoin as a diversifier in portfolios due to its unstable market correlations,” the report said. “We see Bitcoin as a speculative asset and a hedge against monetary easing.”

Top FUD of the Week

New York AG seeks $1.37B from NovaTech founders over Ponzi scheme

New York Attorney General Letitia James has asked a court to order defunct crypto and forex trading platform NovaTech’s founders, Cynthia and Eddy Petion, and related companies to pay $1.37 billion over its Ponzi scheme.

More than 11,000 New Yorkers lost tens of millions of dollars through NovaTech and an earlier crypto mining scheme, AWS Mining, the AG’s office said. The complaint alleged that promoters targeted Haitian and other immigrant communities through prayer groups, social media and WhatsApp, promising high returns and recruitment bonuses.

Bitcoin Core changes security policy as AI makes bugs easier to find

Bitcoin Core is changing how it handles security vulnerabilities, due to how fast large language models can uncover software flaws. 

Bitcoin Core developer Antoine Poinsot said that in the past, vulnerabilities were generally kept under lengthy disclosure embargoes to give users time to upgrade before details became public.

However, Poinsot said LLMs have made some flaws so easy to rediscover that delaying fixes offers little protection.

“The embargo period achieves little but it delays the availability of a fixed release,” said Poinsot. “We are therefore updating our policy disclosure to accommodate those.”

Pentagon bans US forces from using military info to bet in prediction markets

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has barred all Pentagon staff from using undisclosed information to place wagers on upcoming military action, including on prediction market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket. 

In a memo sent to senior Pentagon and defense agencies on Tuesday, Hegseth said all Department of War personnel are prohibited from engaging in financial transactions using nonpublic information. This involves both classified and unclassified information. 

Top Magazine Features of the Week

5 alternatives to Ledger to store your Bitcoin

Hardware wallets aren’t the only way to protect your crypto, but from ETFs and passkeys to multisig accounts, each alternative has its own risks and trade-offs.

Agents can trade 24/7 — but Yat Siu warns you could lose access at any time

The Animoca Brands chairman explains that AI agents can make trades while you sleep, but users need to plan for the day they lose access to the bots.

title: JPMorgan and Wall Street Giants Block AI Agents Over Security Fears
summary: America’s banking giants are drawing a line against autonomous artificial intelligence agents, restricting third-party software from moving customer money without proper authorization. JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup and other financial institutions are confronting a peculiar security problem: AI agents c...
content:
America’s banking giants are drawing a line against autonomous artificial intelligence agents, restricting third-party software from moving customer money without proper authorization. JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup and other financial institutions are confronting a peculiar security problem: AI agents can log in with legitimate credentials but act without clear human approval.

Key Takeaways

  • Reports say JPMorgan, Citi and other major banks are restricting unauthorized AI agents from accessing customer accounts.
  • Binance founder Changpeng Zhao argues that crypto will become a preferred payment system for AI agents.
  • Bitcoin.com News Token Narratives co-host David Sencil warns that aging banking systems could face cyberattacks dwarfing crypto’s losses.

Banks Block AI Agents From Moving Money as Crypto Pushes Ahead

Wall Street has discovered a new kind of customer it doesn’t particularly want: artificial intelligence (AI) software or agents capable of logging into bank accounts and moving money without a human touching the keyboard. JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup and other financial heavyweights are tightening restrictions on third-party AI agents, with unauthorized transactions firmly in their crosshairs.

The crackdown exposes a growing problem for traditional banking: Machines can increasingly operate at financial speed, but banks still depend on security systems designed around human behavior, passwords, and approvals.

Wall Street Draws the Line on Autonomous Banking

Reports published this week describe how major U.S. banks have detected third-party AI agents accessing customer accounts, sometimes using credentials voluntarily supplied by account holders. The catch? A legitimate password doesn’t necessarily mean the account owner approved every subsequent action. Citigroup has explicitly prohibited unauthorized third-party agents from logging in or transacting directly through its digital platforms, while permitting certain approved read-only connections.

JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon sounded the alarm during the bank’s Oct. 13 earnings call, warning against allowing unrestricted outside agents into banking systems because of the risks to customers and the institution. Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan has likewise emphasized human authorization for outgoing payments. Wells Fargo’s updated access agreement, scheduled for Nov. 24, distinguishes between viewing financial information and conducting transactions. The banking industry’s emerging compromise is straightforward: Let approved software examine account information, but don’t hand it the keys to the vault.

Crypto Advocates See an Opening

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao has repeatedly argued that autonomous agents will increasingly bypass traditional finance (TradFi) institutions in favor of cryptocurrency networks. His reasoning centers on speed and accessibility. AI agents don’t naturally fit systems requiring facial recognition, SMS verification, business-hour processing and conventional account applications.

Cryptocurrency wallets, by comparison, can execute programmable transactions continuously, provided their operators control the necessary cryptographic keys. Zhao has suggested that machine-driven payments could eventually dwarf human transaction volumes, potentially reaching one million times their frequency.

Token Narratives Host David Sencil Warns That Aging Banks Face a Bigger Threat

During this week’s Bitcoin.com News’ Token Narratives podcast, David Sencil raised another concern: Artificial intelligence could expose security weaknesses throughout traditional financial infrastructure. Sencil recounted an interview with Gauntlet’s Tarun Chitra, who warned that a major TradFi institution could eventually suffer a devastating breach.

“He said when a traditional finance bank gets hacked, and it’s almost inevitable because of the technology stack is so old,” Sencil explained, pointing to outdated systems that have escaped modernization. Sencil delivered the prediction’s most provocative conclusion:

“It’s going to make anything that’s happened in crypto look like play money.”

An AI Bank Breach Could Make a Blockchain Rollback Look Simple

Consider a hypothetical scenario in which autonomous AI agents compromise half the critical infrastructure of one of America’s largest banks, infiltrating payment systems, internal ledgers, and transaction authorization mechanisms. Millions of unauthorized transfers could potentially occur before security teams can even try to contain the intrusion, forcing the institution to suspend services while investigators determine which transactions are legitimate. The resulting disruption could spread across payment processors, financial counterparties, and international banking networks.

Unlike a blockchain network capable of reverting to an earlier transaction state, a major bank cannot simply rewind its interconnected financial infrastructure. Some payments might have already been settled through the Federal Reserve, while others could have reached foreign institutions or been spent by unsuspecting recipients. Restoring operations could require extensive forensic investigations, transaction reconciliation, regulatory coordination, and potentially billions of dollars in recovery expenses, depending on the damage.

Crowdstrike CEO Warns AI Is Erasing the Hacker Hierarchy

Sencil’s concerns echo warnings from Crowdstrike CEO George Kurtz, who argues that AI is dismantling the traditional hierarchy of cybercriminal capabilities. Speaking in a video clip that’s gone viral on X, Kurtz described a security environment in which sophisticated hacking techniques, once largely reserved for well-funded nation-state operations, are becoming accessible to far less experienced attackers.

The Crowdstrike chief went further, declaring, “The new apex predator is the agent. What I mean by that is this is really the rise of the agent state. We hear about ‘nation state’; it’s now the agent state.”

Crowdstrike’s October intelligence findings add weight to that argument, documenting AI-assisted attacks in which autonomous systems conducted reconnaissance, stole credentials and navigated compromised networks. The firm’s researchers anticipate that declining AI operating costs could make such capabilities increasingly accessible over the next 12 months, although the sophistication of individual attacks will vary.

For banks already grappling with unauthorized AI agents, the implications extend well beyond questionable transactions. Financial institutions must now contend with a technology that can potentially operate on both sides of the security perimeter, assisting legitimate customers while giving attackers increasingly powerful tools.

The irony is difficult to miss: Banks are scrambling to keep autonomous agents from moving money, while cybersecurity executives warn that the same technology is making the people trying to steal it considerably more dangerous.

title: Grayscale Looks Beyond AI Tokens To The Data And Credit Behind Computing
summary: Grayscale's October 23 research note looks at a more specific crypto-and-AI proposition than a general bet on smarter software: who supplies training data, who finances hardware and who receives payment when computing capacity is used.
content:
Grayscale’s October 23 research note looks at a more specific crypto-and-AI proposition than a general bet on smarter software: who supplies training data, who finances hardware and who receives payment when computing capacity is used.

TL;DR

  • The report highlights DATA, USD.AI and Pearl as examples of different infrastructure roles.
  • Hardware financing introduces credit questions alongside blockchain mechanics.
  • A useful service and a valuable token remain separate propositions.

Three business models sit behind one broad AI label

In the note, research head Zach Pandl describes DATA’s work on contributed training data, USD.AI’s GPU-backed lending and Pearl’s attempt to combine AI computing with blockchain rewards. These are Grayscale’s selected examples and expectations, not independently proven outcomes for the entire sector.

Each model has a different customer. A data network needs someone willing to license its datasets. A financing protocol needs borrowers who can service debt. A computing network needs useful workloads and a way to measure delivery. Combining them under an AI-token heading can hide more than it reveals.

USD.AI’s documentation makes the credit element explicit. It describes loans secured by GPUs and associated cash flows, with recourse generally limited to the collateral and specified exceptions. Its yield-bearing instrument draws on loan payments and reserve-related income.

That creates familiar underwriting questions in a new distribution format. What happens if the equipment loses value faster than expected? How concentrated are the customers paying to use it? Who can recover and sell collateral if a borrower fails? A blockchain record can improve visibility into a claim without answering all three.

The operating-versus-financing distinction also runs through Bitdeer’s mining and AI disclosures. Machines, funded capacity and realized customer revenue are related measures, but they are not interchangeable.

The token must connect to the underlying activity

Even successful infrastructure does not automatically deliver the same benefit to every associated token. A governance token, a claim on lending income and a token used to pay for a service can have very different rights.

USD.AI’s depositor guide, for example, separates the non-yield-bearing USDai instrument, the income-accruing sUSDai instrument and CHIP governance. Naming the protocol alone does not identify which exposure a holder receives.

The same discipline applies to data. Paying contributors can encourage useful supply, but sustainable demand depends on whether buyers find that data lawful, relevant and difficult to obtain elsewhere. Token incentives can finance initial activity without proving that customers will keep paying once incentives shrink.

Tokenized-asset growth similarly needs to be read through the rights attached to the token. And AI-facing consumer applications still need users who return because a product is useful.

Grayscale’s report provides a set of business models to examine. Adoption, unit economics and enforceable claims will provide the stronger evidence that those models are becoming durable businesses.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Bitcoin’s 7-Day Hashrate Returns to 1 ZH/s After Nearly 8 Months
summary: Bitcoin’s computational firepower, measured by its network hashrate, has reclaimed the 1 zettahash per second (ZH/s) threshold, with miners worldwide once again executing more than 1 sextillion calculations every second to safeguard the network and compete for newly minted bitcoin. Bitcoin Hashrate ...
content:
Bitcoin’s computational firepower, measured by its network hashrate, has reclaimed the 1 zettahash per second (ZH/s) threshold, with miners worldwide once again executing more than 1 sextillion calculations every second to safeguard the network and compete for newly minted bitcoin.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin’s seven-day average hashrate reclaimed 1 ZH/s for the first time since March 3.
  • More efficient mining hardware and smaller operators are helping offset the industry’s pivot toward AI.
  • Falling hashprice and rising mining difficulty are squeezing miners’ profit margins despite the recovery.

Bitcoin Hashrate Reclaims 1 ZH/s as Mining Power Defies AI Pivot

While bitcoin’s price hovers near $80,000 per coin, miners have propelled the network’s hashrate beyond 1,000 exahash per second (EH/s), equivalent to 1 ZH/s. At press time, the network’s hashrate stands at 1,080.23 EH/s, or 1.08023 ZH/s, following its latest difficulty adjustment roughly nine days ago at block height 971712.

Moreover, the seven-day average recently reclaimed the 1 ZH/s threshold for the first time since March 3. Curiously, this resurgence comes as several major mining firms redirect equipment and capital toward artificial intelligence (AI) and other high-performance computing ventures. Meanwhile, smaller, solo, and privately held mining operations appear to be filling the void, sustaining Bitcoin’s expanding computational power.

Next-Generation Mining Hardware Seemingly Helped Offset AI Exodus

Despite the industry’s pivot toward AI, advances in bitcoin mining hardware over the past two years have delivered faster, more energy-efficient machines, providing miners with a valuable competitive buffer. Today’s most advanced Bitcoin mining rigs can execute hundreds of trillions of calculations per second. Some models now surpass 1 petahash per second (PH/s), equivalent to 1,000 terahash per second (TH/s).

Mining efficiency is measured in joules per terahash (J/TH), a metric that reveals how much energy a machine consumes to perform a given amount of computational work. In simple terms, the lower the figure, the less electricity required to deliver the same hashing output. Several next-generation machines manufactured by companies such as Bitmain and MicroBT now operate below 10 J/TH, offering a substantial economic advantage over their aging predecessors.

Falling Hashprice and Rising Difficulty Will Test Miners’ Profit Margins

Although Bitcoin’s hashrate has reclaimed the 1 ZH/s threshold, it remains below its previous peaks of approximately 1.3 to 1.44 ZH/s, despite recovering substantially from July’s low near 726 exahash per second (EH/s). Several headwinds could still constrain the network’s computational expansion, with BTC’s market price representing the most consequential variable. Bitcoin’s U.S. dollar valuation has declined over the past 30 days, placing additional downward pressure on hashprice.

Hashprice measures mining revenue by calculating the market value of a given amount of computational power over a 24-hour period. Currently, hashprice stands at $36.04 per petahash per second (PH/s) per day, down from $40.42 on Sept. 25, 2026, according to hashrateindex.com stats. Compounding that pressure, mining difficulty climbed another 5.92% during the latest adjustment. Nevertheless, miners have maintained their momentum, with blocks arriving at an average interval of 9 minutes and 31 seconds over the past 24 hours.

That accelerated pace suggests the next difficulty adjustment, expected Oct. 29, will likely bring another increase. Still, Bitcoin’s hashrate recovery suggests advances in hardware efficiency are more than compensating for the migration of capital and expertise, offering an encouraging indication of the network’s resilience.

Yet with hashprice declining and mining difficulty climbing, the smaller private operators filling the gap may be contending with considerably tighter profit margins than the headline hashrate figures suggest. Only time will tell.

title: Lido Puts Liquidity Buffers At The Center Of Ethereum ETP Yield Debate
summary: An Ethereum investment product can advertise staking exposure without putting every unit of its ETH to work. Lido's October 23 comparison of European exchange-traded products brings attention to the cash-management choices behind the reward figures investors see.
content:
An Ethereum investment product can advertise staking exposure without putting every unit of its ETH to work. Lido’s October 23 comparison of European exchange-traded products brings attention to the cash-management choices behind the reward figures investors see.

TL;DR

  • Lido argues that staking allocation, fees and liquidity management shape ETP rewards.
  • Native staking withdrawals depend on network processes and queues.
  • A transferable staking token adds a market exit route, with its own execution risks.

The reward rate applies to the capital actually earning it

In its new institutional note, Lido says products holding an unstaked liquidity buffer may earn rewards on less than their full ETH exposure. It promotes liquid staking as an alternative and uses WisdomTree’s stETH-backed product as an example. Lido has a commercial interest in that comparison.

The arithmetic is straightforward even without ranking any funds. In an illustrative product with 100 ETH, a 20 ETH unstaked buffer would leave 80 ETH generating staking rewards. If the staked portion earned 3% over a year, it would produce 2.4 ETH before fees and other adjustments. Those are hypothetical inputs, not a forecast or a quoted product return.

A buffer is not necessarily wasted capital. It can provide liquidity when redemptions arrive or when other processes take time. The useful question is what operational benefit the buffer buys and how much reward the product gives up in exchange.

Ethereum’s withdrawal documentation explains that exiting validators pass through network processes and that demand can affect the timeline. A fund’s need to meet a commercial deadline does not accelerate the underlying protocol queue.

Liquid staking replaces one constraint with another market

A transferable claim on staked ETH can be sold without waiting for every underlying validator to exit. But a sale needs buyers at an acceptable price. Transferability does not guarantee that a large transaction will execute at the value used in a fund’s accounting.

During ordinary trading, market makers may bridge that gap efficiently. Under stress, the amount of available liquidity and the cost of absorbing an order become more important. A structure that supports full staking can still face a difficult execution decision when many holders seek liquidity together.

The broader point echoes Bitcoin products using options for downside management: the underlying asset’s name cannot fully describe the investor’s payout.

Likewise, the process examined in CoinShares’ fund liquidation shows why redemption rules deserve attention before a deadline arrives. Trading a share and withdrawing its underlying exposure are distinct operations.

NewsBTC’s coverage of corporate Ethereum staking adds another comparison: an equity holder owns a company with financing and management decisions, rather than a simple balance of staked coins.

Lido’s note is therefore most useful as a prompt to examine the complete structure. Allocation, net reward sharing, liquidity arrangements and market depth must be read together before two headline staking rates can be meaningfully compared.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Evernorth Seeks to Register 5.2M Shares as It Plans More XRP Purchases
summary: Evernorth’s new share-sale arrangement could provide approximately $80.7 million in gross funding to support its XRP treasury. The company intends to put any proceeds toward additional purchases, alongside other corporate uses. Cantor Deal Could Support More XRP Purchases Additional funding for XRP ...
content:
Evernorth’s new share-sale arrangement could provide approximately $80.7 million in gross funding to support its XRP treasury. The company intends to put any proceeds toward additional purchases, alongside other corporate uses.

Key Takeaways

  • The registration request covers up to 5,218,935 shares for Cantor’s resale.
  • Potential funding depends on share prices and use of the facility.
  • Evernorth agreed to a $521,893.50 nonrefundable upfront commitment fee.

Cantor Deal Could Support More XRP Purchases

Additional funding for XRP purchases could come through a share-sale arrangement that Evernorth Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: XRPN) established Oct. 23. The XRP treasury company filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to register potential resales by CF Principal Investments LLC, referred to as Cantor, an affiliate of Cantor Fitzgerald & Co.

Its planned share sales to Cantor could generate approximately $80.7 million gross, assuming all 5,218,935 shares sell at the Oct. 22 closing price of $15.46. Evernorth estimated up to $78.3 million net after fees and expenses over approximately 14 months. Actual receipts depend on future sale prices and facility use.

The company stated:

“We intend to purchase additional XRP and increase our overall holdings of XRP in the future.”

Management retains discretion over allocating proceeds among acquisitions, XRP ecosystem activities, and working capital, or funds for day-to-day operations.

Financing Terms Set Costs and Purchase Limits

Once registration becomes effective and other conditions are satisfied, Evernorth can direct Cantor to buy newly issued shares. Cantor generally pays 97% of the volume-weighted average price, which weights trades by size. Evernorth receives proceeds from those sales; money from subsequent resales goes to Cantor.

Under the agreement, the $521,893.50 upfront commitment fee is nonrefundable even if Cantor makes no purchases. Recalculation can increase total commitment fees to $1 million. Purchases are generally limited to 20% of trading volume during the applicable period and cannot push Cantor’s beneficial ownership above 4.99%.

A separate mechanism involves public warrants exercisable for Evernorth stock, which give holders the right, but not the obligation, to buy shares at $11.50 each. As of Oct. 22, up to 9,283,847 shares were issuable through Evernorth’s outstanding warrants, so full cash exercise could provide approximately $106.8 million to the company. That funding depends on holders exercising their rights.

Treasury Plans Link XRP Purchases With Deployment

Following its Nasdaq debut with approximately 473 million XRP on Oct. 12, Evernorth aims to increase XRP per share. Issuance through either financing mechanism would dilute existing investors’ ownership percentages unless they acquire more stock. Progress toward the treasury objective depends on token holdings growing relative to outstanding shares.

Stockholders own an interest in the business, whose assets include XRP held as part of its corporate treasury. Direct cryptocurrency ownership instead gives the holder exposure to the digital asset itself.

An Oct. 14 announcement named Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase, and Bitgo as institutional execution partners for strategies scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter. Partnership agreements remain subject to customary closing conditions and required regulatory and corporate approvals. Initial activities would use established institutional counterparties.

Later phases of its planned XRP treasury deployment would involve native lending and credit markets, allowing borrowing and lending through features built into the XRP Ledger. Evernorth intends to participate as validators activate those capabilities and they demonstrate reliability in production.

title: Lido Opens Higher-Balance Ethereum Validators With A Deliberately Small Start
summary: Lido has opened a permissionless route to Ethereum validators that can hold much larger effective balances, but the first allocation is deliberately limited. Its October 23 launch of 0x02 Community Staking Module separates gaining access from receiving the full amount of stake a validator could even...
content:
Lido has opened a permissionless route to Ethereum validators that can hold much larger effective balances, but the first allocation is deliberately limited. Its October 23 launch of 0x02 Community Staking Module separates gaining access from receiving the full amount of stake a validator could eventually support.

TL;DR

  • Lido says its new 0x02 CSM is live.
  • Operators supply a bond while protocol allocations arrive in stages.
  • Existing 0x01 operators can continue without switching modules.

A larger validator is funded through two queues

The launch announcement sets the bond at 32 ETH for the first key and 30 ETH for each additional key. Lido supplies the allocated stake. New keys first receive a 32 ETH seed deposit; further deposits follow after activation through a separate top-up queue.

The module starts with a 0.01% share limit of Lido Core’s total value locked and 32 top-up seats. Further capacity increases depend on a staged governance process and sufficient protocol inflows. A maximum balance is therefore a technical ceiling, not an immediate allocation promise to every operator.

The Ethereum change underneath this is EIP-7251, which allows a validator’s effective balance to rise to 2,048 ETH while retaining a lower activation requirement. More stake can consequently be represented by fewer validator keys.

For an operator, fewer keys can simplify parts of administration. It also makes the amount controlled by each operational setup more consequential. Key count alone becomes a weaker way to judge how broadly stake is distributed.

That distinction fits the concentration questions examined in NewsBTC’s network-resilience coverage. Independent operators, infrastructure diversity and correlated failures all matter alongside the number of validators.

The entry bond is only one part of the operating decision

An operator’s experience depends on how long a key waits for activation, how quickly additional stake arrives and how reliably the validator performs. A favorable projection at full allocation cannot describe the whole period between posting a bond and reaching that allocation.

The comparison with solo staking also requires care. A bonded operator receiving protocol stake and a solo staker providing all the capital are taking different roles. The same percentage headline can conceal different denominators, duties and sources of reward.

Large corporate ETH treasuries illustrate how staking decisions can involve substantial balances. The new CSM route instead concerns how independent operators can service stake allocated through Lido.

It is separate, too, from Ethereum’s execution-capacity tests. Supporting larger validators does not by itself raise the volume of application transactions a block can carry.

The staged launch gives the market concrete milestones to observe: activated keys, completed top-ups and approved capacity increases. Those measurements will show whether the permissionless route is expanding in practice, beyond the largest balance allowed by its design.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Hackers Breach GMO Trading Cloud, Putting 26,739 Servers at Risk
summary: Hackers infiltrated a Japanese cloud trading service, exposing as many as 26,739 servers to potential compromise and allegedly hijacking brokerage accounts to execute unauthorized trades. The attackers then demanded money, threatening further financial damage if the company refused to pay. Attackers...
content:
Hackers infiltrated a Japanese cloud trading service, exposing as many as 26,739 servers to potential compromise and allegedly hijacking brokerage accounts to execute unauthorized trades. The attackers then demanded money, threatening further financial damage if the company refused to pay.

Key Takeaways

  • GMO Internet identified a cloud security breach potentially affecting 26,739 trading servers.
  • Hackers threatened GMO customers’ accounts at more than 70 brokerages unless their demands were met.
  • GMO Internet rejected the extortion demand and offered compensation for verified unauthorized trading losses.

Attackers Target Always-On Trading Servers

GMO Internet discovered the intrusion after a customer inquiry on Oct. 19, 2026. By Oct. 20, investigators had confirmed malicious software inside customer server environments operated by Onamae.com Desktop Cloud, a service designed to keep automated foreign exchange (FX) trading programs running around the clock.

The platform supports trading software such as Metatrader 4 and Metatrader 5, allowing customers to execute strategies without leaving their personal computers running. Unfortunately, that convenience also placed valuable brokerage credentials inside an environment that attackers had penetrated.

GMO began shutting down servers at 4 a.m. Japan time on Oct. 21, eventually taking the entire service offline. The company subsequently identified a security flaw in its own systems that permitted unauthorized access and the removal of customer information.

Hackers Threaten Accounts at More Than 70 Brokerages

The attackers allegedly obtained trading credentials and used compromised accounts to execute unauthorized transactions. Reports described customers losing substantial sums within minutes, including one account of approximately 2.4 million yen disappearing through repeated trades in roughly 84 seconds.

The extortion demand took an especially aggressive turn. Attackers threatened further unauthorized activity affecting customer accounts at more than 70 domestic and international securities and FX brokerages unless GMO paid. They also threatened to expose stolen information and launch additional ransomware attacks.

GMO refused, arguing that payment offered no guarantee stolen information would disappear or that further attacks would stop. The company consulted police and engaged outside cybersecurity specialists. Importantly, the 26,739 figure represents potentially exposed servers, not confirmed infections. The total financial damage remains undetermined.

GMO’s Cryptocurrency History

GMO Internet Group has deep roots in the cryptocurrency industry, having entered the sector during bitcoin’s explosive growth in 2017. The Japanese conglomerate launched GMO Coin in May of that year, later securing regulatory registration and expanding into ethereum, bitcoin cash, litecoin and XRP trading. That September, GMO unveiled ambitious bitcoin mining plans involving renewable-powered facilities in Northern Europe, proprietary 7-nanometer mining chips and cloud mining services. GMO even paid employees in BTC in 2017.

The venture ultimately proved expensive, with the company recording approximately 35.5 billion yen in restructuring-related losses in 2018 as falling cryptocurrency prices battered mining profitability. Despite that setback, GMO continued building its digital asset business through GMO Coin, adding lending, staking, margin trading and token offerings. The group also explored stablecoins, blockchain ventures and investments in emerging cryptocurrency businesses, establishing a substantial presence in Japan’s digital asset economy.

The Japanese Heavyweight Responds to the Attack

Regarding the latest cyberattack, GMO announced on Oct. 24 that every existing Desktop Cloud customer would receive a flat 5,000-yen payment, regardless of whether they suffered financial losses. The company also pledged to compensate verified losses and associated fees from unauthorized trading, while offering affected customers six months of free access to an alternative desktop platform.

GMO rejected the attackers’ extortion demands, engaged outside cybersecurity specialists and submitted evidence to Japanese police. Group founder Masatoshi Kumagai also requested government intervention under Japan’s active cyber defense framework, seeking assistance in neutralizing the threat. The compromised infrastructure remains offline as investigators work to determine the full extent of the intrusion, the number of affected accounts and the financial damage inflicted on customers.

title: Binance Founder CZ Makes Shocking Claim About AI Hacking: “No Crypto Wallet Is 100% Safe”
summary: Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao has warned crypto users against assuming any wallet is completely secure, arguing that artificial intelligence could intensify security threats without breaking blockchain cryptography.
content:
Skip to content

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao has warned crypto users against assuming any wallet is completely secure, arguing that artificial intelligence could intensify security threats without breaking blockchain cryptography.

The comments followed two X posts in which CZ discussed the limits of digital security and AI risks, highlighting phishing and social engineering as potential threats to crypto holders.

CZ Warns of AI-Driven Crypto Security Risks

On October 23, Zhao challenged concerns that artificial intelligence could directly compromise Bitcoin’s cryptographic protections. He argued that fears about AI hacking cryptocurrency networks overlook the risks facing traditional internet and financial systems.

AI can threaten crypto holders through sophisticated phishing and social engineering attacks that exploit leaked personal data without compromising core cryptography. Source: @cz_binance via X

“Everyone worried about AI hacking crypto, but the internet and banking systems rely on weaker encryption,” CZ wrote.

He also explained how attackers could exploit AI without having to defeat the cryptography protecting digital assets. “AI doesn’t need to break Bitcoin’s cryptography to cause damage; leaked data already enables more phishing, social engineering, etc.,” he added, ending the post with “Stay SAFU.”

The distinction is important. AI-assisted attacks can use personal information exposed through data breaches to create convincing messages, impersonate trusted contacts, or imitate legitimate customer-support teams. A victim who follows a fraudulent link or reveals a wallet recovery phrase can lose funds even when the underlying blockchain and its cryptographic systems remain uncompromised.

Zhao’s comparison between crypto encryption and the protections used by banks and internet services should not be treated as a universal technical assessment. Security depends on the specific algorithms, implementations, account safeguards, and methods used to protect sensitive information.

Recent Hardware Wallet Incidents Highlight Self-Custody Risks

Zhao’s warning comes amid two separate hardware-wallet security incidents reported in 2026. The cases illustrate how cryptocurrency can be stolen through weaknesses in a device’s supply chain or software, rather than through a direct attack on a blockchain’s cryptographic foundations.

CryptoBilis faces scrutiny after researchers linked a hardware wallet incident to over $90 million in crypto losses. Source: Bloomberg via X

In October, Ledger investigated cryptocurrency thefts linked to devices sold through CryptoBilis, a Southeast Asian reseller. Blockchain analytics firms estimated that the incident involved approximately $93 million to $95 million in stolen assets, although the figures were not confirmed as a final loss total by Ledger.

Ledger confirmed finding an unauthorized hardware implant in at least one affected device. Reports indicated that the tampered hardware could capture users’ recovery phrases during setup and transmit the information to attackers. Tether subsequently froze $10 million in USDT linked to the thefts, according to published reports.

A separate incident involving Coldcard Bitcoin hardware wallets demonstrated a different type of vulnerability. A flaw in seed generation affected certain devices and reduced the randomness protecting wallet keys, potentially making affected wallets vulnerable to brute-force attacks.

TRM Labs reported in August that the exploit had drained approximately 1,816 BTC, worth about $116 million at the time, from more than 5,200 addresses. The vulnerability originated in older firmware, meaning that installing an update alone would not repair recovery phrases generated under the affected conditions.

Neither incident establishes that AI cracked Bitcoin’s cryptography. Instead, they show how implementation errors, compromised hardware, and weaknesses in wallet setup can expose assets even when users choose tools designed for offline storage.

Why No Crypto Wallet Is Completely Safe

On October 22, Zhao published a broader security reminder stating, “No crypto wallet is 100% safe. No software is bug-free. No tech is 100% secure.”

He also noted that risk exists in both action and inaction, urging users to stay informed, manage risk, and address problems as they arise. The message reflects an important distinction in cryptocurrency security: controlling private keys directly removes reliance on an exchange for custody, but it also places greater responsibility on the wallet owner.

CZ issued a crypto security warning amid reported 2026 hardware wallet incidents involving a Ledger supply-chain attack and a Coldcard firmware flaw, highlighting risks beyond core cryptography. Source: @cz_binance via X

A self-custody wallet does not store cryptocurrency in the same way a physical wallet holds cash. Instead, it manages the private keys or recovery information required to authorize transactions recorded on the blockchain. Anyone who obtains the necessary credentials may be able to transfer the assets, and blockchain transactions generally cannot be reversed simply because a user was deceived.

Hardware wallets can reduce exposure to internet-connected devices, but they are not immune to manufacturing defects, compromised distribution channels, or flawed software. Similarly, software wallets can be affected by malicious applications, device malware, and stolen credentials. The appropriate level of protection depends on how the wallet is created, stored, accessed, and maintained.

Using a centralized exchange introduces a different set of trade-offs. Customers rely on the platform’s custody controls and operational security, while self-custody gives users direct control but requires them to protect their own keys and backups. Neither approach eliminates every form of risk.

How Crypto Holders Can Reduce AI Hacking Risks

Zhao’s warning points to practical precautions rather than a guarantee of perfect security. Users should treat unexpected messages, urgent account warnings and unsolicited requests to verify a wallet with caution, even when the communication appears professionally written or refers to personal details.

Recovery phrases and private keys should never be shared with another person, entered into an unfamiliar website, or sent through email and messaging services. Users should also verify official website addresses, avoid installing wallet applications from untrusted sources, and consider phishing-resistant authentication methods, including compatible hardware security keys, for accounts that support them.

Hardware-wallet buyers should use the manufacturer’s official store or a trusted, authorized distributor and inspect devices for signs of tampering. If a device or recovery phrase may have been compromised, simply updating its software may not be sufficient. Moving assets to a wallet created with a new, secure recovery phrase may be necessary, provided the transfer is carried out safely.

Regularly reviewing security guidance and keeping devices updated can help reduce exposure to known vulnerabilities. However, users should understand what an update fixes and whether existing keys or recovery phrases remain at risk.

CZ’s central message is that cryptocurrency security requires ongoing attention, not blind confidence in a particular device or technology. As AI tools become more capable, the immediate concern for many holders may be increasingly convincing fraud and the exploitation of personal information, rather than an attacker directly breaking blockchain encryption.
