title: Bank Lobby Presses OCC For Clarity On Stablecoin Rewards After Final Rule
summary: A final stablecoin rule has not ended the argument over rewards. The Bank Policy Institute used its October 24 newsletter to renew criticism of how the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency will judge arrangements that pay stablecoin holders through third parties.
content:
A final stablecoin rule has not ended the argument over rewards. The Bank Policy Institute used its October 24 newsletter to renew criticism of how the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency will judge arrangements that pay stablecoin holders through third parties.

TL;DR

  • BPI says case-by-case decisions leave stablecoin reward arrangements unclear.
  • The dispute concerns implementation of the issuer yield prohibition.
  • The OCC says its broader GENIUS Act rule takes effect January 18, 2027.

The disagreement is about how the prohibition is applied

In the newsletter, BPI repeated its October 21 response to the final rule. The banking trade group objects to removal of a proposed presumption covering certain issuer arrangements with third parties. It says the replacement approach lacks a clear process for explaining decisions and making outcomes public.

This is a lobbying position from an organization representing banks. Its concern about deposits moving into stablecoins is a forecast about competitive and financial effects, rather than evidence that the newly finalized rule has already caused a measurable outflow.

The OCC’s announcement presents the rule as a framework covering reserve backing, redemption and risk management. It confirms the January effective date and says separate work will address anti-money-laundering and sanctions requirements. BPI’s criticism addresses one part of that wider framework.

The practical distinction is between a payment token’s reserve income and a customer incentive offered elsewhere in its distribution chain. Identifying who pays, who ultimately funds the payment and what behavior earns it can matter more than whether a product calls the transfer a reward, rebate or yield.

Product design now has a regulatory interpretation problem

Consider two hypothetical offers: a payment app discounts a purchase, while another pays a recurring amount for keeping tokens idle. Both benefit the user, but their commercial purpose, funding and connection to the issuer may differ. Their labels alone cannot establish their treatment under the rule.

That is why published reasoning would be useful beyond the banks lobbying for it. A decision about one arrangement can help other providers understand which features the regulator regarded as decisive. Without that detail, firms may struggle to compare their own structures with earlier cases.

The product boundaries are already becoming more complex. SoFi’s tokenized-deposit plan raises a different set of claims from a payment stablecoin, even when conversion makes the customer experience look continuous.

Meanwhile, stablecoin payment activity measures how tokens are used, not whether an incentive is legally permissible. Operational activity cannot answer the policy question by itself.

The scrutiny of transaction purpose also connects with wallet and financial-crime controls: the institution still needs to understand the economic relationship behind the transfer. For the OCC dispute, the next useful evidence will be supervisory guidance and disclosed decisions, rather than competing descriptions of what the rule should mean.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $138M as Zcash Extends 3-Day Inflow Streak
summary: U.S. bitcoin ETFs closed Friday with $137.94 million in net outflows, capping a volatile week in which large inflows were quickly followed by equally sharp reversals. Ether returned to modest inflows, while Zcash and NEAR remained the only other categories to attract fresh capital. Bitcoin ETFs Swin...
content:
U.S. bitcoin ETFs closed Friday with $137.94 million in net outflows, capping a volatile week in which large inflows were quickly followed by equally sharp reversals. Ether returned to modest inflows, while Zcash and NEAR remained the only other categories to attract fresh capital.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin ETFs lost $137.94M on Friday after $1B+ of early-week inflows reversed sharply.
  • Ether returned to modest inflows, while zcash extended its rebound with $20.52M.
  • The week showed that institutional crypto demand remains active but highly tactical and selective.

Bitcoin ETFs Swing From Inflows to Selling

Bitcoin ETF demand ended the week on a softer note.

The group lost $137.94 million, led by a $110.34 million outflow from Blackrock’s IBIT. Fidelity’s FBTC shed another $31.78 million. Morgan Stanley’s MSBT provided the only inflow at $4.19 million.

Trading value fell to $1.33 billion, while net assets closed at $104.43 billion.

The lower turnover is notable after Thursday’s $635.49 million withdrawal. It suggests the most aggressive round of de-risking may have passed, though institutional appetite for bitcoin clearly remains fragile.

For bitcoin’s price, the week showed how quickly ETF flows can move from strong accumulation to broad profit-taking.

Bitcoin’s Midweek Surge Loses Momentum

The broader pattern is more important than Friday’s number alone.

Bitcoin ETFs attracted more than $1 billion across Monday through Wednesday. Then came two sharp reversals: $635.49 million left Thursday and another $137.94 million exited Friday.

That sequence highlights how tactical current positioning has become.

Blackrock and Fidelity dominated both sides of the trade, first driving inflows and then accounting for much of the selling. The result is a market where large institutions are still active, but conviction is not yet strong enough to prevent rapid reversals.

Ether Finds a Rare Clean Inflow Day

Ether ETFs managed a modest $4.35 million net inflow.

Fidelity’s FETH attracted $3.58 million, while Morgan Stanley’s MSSE added $773,440. No ether fund recorded an outflow.

Trading activity totaled $392.93 million, with net assets closing at $14.64 billion.

The clean positive session is significant after weeks of persistent redemptions. Still, the size of the inflow remains small relative to recent withdrawals. That makes Friday more of a stabilization signal than a decisive shift in ethereum demand across the crypto ETF market.

Zcash Extends Its Rebound

Zcash ETFs remained one of the strongest pockets of demand. Grayscale’s ZCSH attracted $20.52 million, marking a third straight day of inflows. Net assets climbed to $706.72 million.

NEAR ETFs also stayed positive, with Bitwise’s NRR adding $992,690. XRP, solana and HYPE ETFs recorded no net flows.

That quiet finish suggests higher-beta demand remains selective even as some smaller products continue to attract targeted capital.

The product pipeline is also expanding.

Franklin Templeton has registered two new Nasdaq-listed ETFs, built around a 95% U.S. equity and 5% bitcoin allocation. Dividends from the equity portion would be directed into bitcoin exposure, with quarterly rebalancing designed to manage the allocation.

The structure is another sign that bitcoin is moving deeper into traditional portfolio construction rather than remaining confined to standalone crypto products.

Friday’s flows therefore closed the week with a mixed message: bitcoin demand softened, ether stabilized, and Zcash continued to draw capital. Institutional participation remains active, but increasingly selective.

title: Kraken Lists SFI As Saffron Puts Uniswap Trading Fees At The Center Of Its Product
summary: Kraken added SFI trading on October 23, bringing fresh exchange access to a token attached to a protocol that has changed substantially since its early DeFi incarnation. Saffron's current product separates an upfront payment from the uncertain trading fees generated by a Uniswap liquidity position.
content:
Kraken added SFI trading on October 23, bringing fresh exchange access to a token attached to a protocol that has changed substantially since its early DeFi incarnation. Saffron’s current product separates an upfront payment from the uncertain trading fees generated by a Uniswap liquidity position.

TL;DR

  • Kraken says SFI trading is live, subject to geographic restrictions.
  • Saffron’s current vaults exchange potential future Uniswap fees for an upfront premium.
  • Buying the governance token does not itself create a claim on a particular vault’s yield.

Today’s Saffron is built around a fee swap

The listing announcement identifies SFI, also called Spice, as an Ethereum token used in Saffron governance. It expressly distinguishes the current vault system from the project’s retired tranche and insurance mechanisms. App and instant-purchase availability also depend on liquidity conditions.

According to Saffron’s vault documentation, one participant supplies the assets for a Uniswap position and receives an upfront premium. Participants on the other side pay that premium in return for the fees the position produces during an agreed term.

The transaction rearranges uncertainty. The liquidity supplier knows the premium received, while the fee buyer takes exposure to the amount of trading activity that ultimately passes through the position. A predetermined premium does not turn the entire underlying asset position into a fixed-value deposit.

Uniswap’s documentation explains why the selected price range matters: a position outside its range stops earning fees. The position’s token composition can also change as traders move the market through that range.

That makes order routing relevant. The external liquidity connections in NewsBTC’s Aggregator Hooks coverage concern where transactions execute, which ultimately influences which liquidity providers collect fees.

Exchange access does not settle the token’s economics

Three things now sit beside one another: a traded governance token, a protocol offering fee swaps and the liquidity positions underneath those swaps. They should be assessed separately. An exchange listing makes the token easier to access for eligible customers; it does not demonstrate demand for the vaults or establish a direct entitlement to their cash flows.

A vault’s results depend on its term, premium, underlying pair and price range. Even a busy market can disappoint a fee buyer if the relevant liquidity spends much of its time outside the active range. Equally, a premium that looks attractive to one side is a cost the other side must overcome.

The distinction between access and economic exposure also appears in structured Bitcoin fund proposals. The wrapper’s name says less than its actual payout rules.

And as BTF’s wind-down demonstrates, familiar tickers can persist while the claims behind them change. SFI’s new listing is a reason to examine Saffron’s current documentation, rather than rely on descriptions of its original 2020 design.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: 22 Companies Block OKXICE Tokenized Stocks, Putting 63-Share Crypto Plan Under Pressure
summary:
Key Takeaways: A total of twenty-two companies have declined to accept tokenization of their shares on the pending OKXICE. Among the most recent rejecters are Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and
The post 22 Companies Block OKXICE Tokenized Stocks, Putting 63-Share Crypto Plan Under Pressure appeared first...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • A total of twenty-two companies have declined to accept tokenization of their shares on the pending OKXICE.
  • Among the most recent rejecters are Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and Intuit.
  • The SEC has established an innovation exemption that will effectively bar tokenization listings of stocks, which will impose an obstacle to tokenizing stocks.

One of crypto’s most ambitious initiatives to bring traditional stocks onto the blockchain is now under attack from a group of large companies.

In total, OKX and Intercontinental Exchange, the parent of the New York Stock Exchange, intended to have 63 stocks tokenized via their joint venture OKXICE. It has been met with resistance from nearly a third of the proposed issuers now, however.

  • 22 Companies Push Back Against OKXICE Tokenized Stocks
  • Issuers Now Hold a Direct Veto
    • Crypto’s 24/7 Stock Trading Push Hits a Corporate Wall

22 Companies Push Back Against OKXICE Tokenized Stocks

Six additional companies, including Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and Intuit, have objected to having tokenized versions of their shares listed on OKXICE, according to regulatory documents reviewed by Reuters.

The new complaints bring the total number of companies to 22. Other companies that have refused to join include Microsoft and Alphabet. Sixteen of the companies are listed on Nasdaq, and the other 6 on NYSE. The reasons behind the objections by the individual companies are not identified in the filings.

This is because under the SEC’s new rules, issuer approval essentially constitutes a gatekeeper. Platforms have the right to inform companies of their plan to offer tokenized stock, but they are not allowed to do so if the company objects within the designated time.

Read More: OKX Marketing Chief Haider Rafique Steps Back After Seven Years at Crypto Exchange

Issuers Now Hold a Direct Veto

The SEC’s September “innovation exemption” was crafted to provide a regulated avenue for tokenization on the National Market System.

The temporary framework should maintain the same rights and privileges that attach to a security, such as dividends and voting rights. Even before 3rd party tokenized shares trade, Tokenized trading venues will afford issuers a formal opportunity to object.

What that protection offers distinguishes the U.S. version from many offshore tokenized-stock products, during which investors can only obtain synthetic exposure however no actual voter rights.

Crypto’s 24/7 Stock Trading Push Hits a Corporate Wall

The tokenization champion has been touted as a means of permitting immediate trading, quicker settlement, and programmable market construction.

The SEC has definitely given a license to experiment. OKXICE is already registered as one of the firms that announced they will be operating under the tokenized securities exemption. Only regulatory approval does not mean that the issuer will be willing to participate.

As far as OKXICE is concerned, 22 objections to a projected universe of 63 stocks are quite a commercial challenge. The platform could still open up for firms that aren’t opposed, though the platform’s sales momentum could be soured if major issuers continue to decline.

The move also underscores a larger conflict within tokenized finance: crypto companies would like to introduce traditional securities onto the blockchain, but issuers are worried about all of the implications behind fragmented liquidity, price discovery and onchain trading in securities markets.

title: Initia Halts L1 and Rollups After $2.7M Exploit Tied to Unauthorized Token Minting
summary:
Key Takeaways: After facing a security incident due to unauthorized token mints, Initia has suspended its Layer 1 and has integrated rollups onto its network. Initial estimates of the attacker’s
The post Initia Halts L1 and Rollups After $2.7M Exploit Tied to Unauthorized Token Minting appeared firs...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • After facing a security incident due to unauthorized token mints, Initia has suspended its Layer 1 and has integrated rollups onto its network.
  • Initial estimates of the attacker’s outflow from the AUSD, ETH and USDC projects hover around $2.7 million.
  • Full effects are not confirmed and Initia stated it was working with the validators, exchanges, and security teams.

Initia has suspended its blockchain infrastructure after an exploit reportedly allowed an attacker to mint unbacked tokens and move millions of dollars in crypto to Ethereum.

As of Oct 23, 2026, 3:41:30 PM UTC, the Initia L1 and Rollups have been halted due to a security incident.

Our team is actively investigating the situation and working to establish the full scope of any impact with security teams, validators, and exchanges.

We will share verified information through our official channels as it becomes available.

Please remain cautious of unofficial links, messages, or claims circulating during this time.

— Initia 🪢 (@initia) October 23, 2026

As investigators dig into the damage, the network halt started at 3:41:30 p.m. UTC on Oct. 23, including the Initia Layer 1 network and its rollup network.

  • Initia Network Halt Follows Unauthorized Token Minting
  • Exploit Reportedly Targeted AUSD
    • INIT Price Rebounds Despite Security Scare
    • Initia Investigates Scope Before Restarting Network

Initia Network Halt Follows Unauthorized Token Minting

Blockchain security researcher, Spreek, first spotted the incident, stated that one attacker had “infiniminted” tokens and is already shorting out around $2.6 million, with more funds on the way.

Later Initia acknowledged the security incident but not the exact vulnerability nor the amount that was lost. The team, in collaboration with security engineers, validators and exchanges, was investigating the extent of the hack.

The latest preliminary remarks by Initia founder Ezaan Mangalji hinted that a previously unidentified bug is present in MoveVM’s Cosmos SDK implementation. The issue has allowed unauthorized token minting, but has not impacted native INIT tokens, he said. We are told that the attacker has reportedly tapped $2.7 million worth of AUSD, ETH and USDC before the chain is suspended.

Read More: Bitget Halts Withdrawals After $351.6M Hot Wallet Incident Hits Crypto Exchange

Exploit Reportedly Targeted AUSD

The hacker used the Move-related vulnerability to create 2 million AUSD without the necessary support, according to D2 Finance.

They found that approximately 1.4 million AUSD, 105 ETH and 1.08 million USDC were also transferred to Ethereum later on, through the platform. The money was then swept into an Ethereum wallet, per the incident report paraphrased by the crypto researchers.

Initia has not independently verified all those numbers yet, and the final loss estimate could vary as more details become available in the investigation.

INIT Price Rebounds Despite Security Scare

At first the exploit had their way with INIT, but the token quickly bounced back. According to CoinGecko data, INIT’s price has hovered around $0.148 during the past 24 hours, trading by approximately $0.114 to $0.156 over that period. As it became one of the hot market events, trading volume also rose significantly.

That bounce has occurred despite the network not being terminated, implying some traders were viewing the reported minting bug as distinct from the INIT native token.

Initia Investigates Scope Before Restarting Network

The core of Initia is its Layer 1-based mainnet, which will feature connected application-specific rollups, commonly known as Minitias. Stopping any base chain and rollups helps affect a wider ecosystem than just stopping one application.

Restart timeline not announced for the project. It has also not yet issued a definitive report on the extent of the damage to the assets, the losses of the users, nor clear action for remediation.

In the meantime, the main questions are if the vulnerability applied to just one function in MoveVM, to see if it had let more tokens out of the ecosystem, and to determine the extent of the loss until the validators halted the chain.

title: China Sets 2030 Deadline for National Blockchain Network Despite Sweeping Crypto Ban
summary:
Key Takeaways: Under the new 5-year digital strategy, China aims to achieve a national blockchain network which will be largely completed by 2030. The plan involves increased blockchain adoption, enhanced
The post China Sets 2030 Deadline for National Blockchain Network Despite Sweeping Crypto Ban a...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Under the new 5-year digital strategy, China aims to achieve a national blockchain network which will be largely completed by 2030.
  • The plan involves increased blockchain adoption, enhanced technological protocols and deeper integration with digital infrastructures.
  • Beijing’s blockchain initiative isn’t a rethink, crypto company business is not permitted in the mainland.

Back in the national digital infrastructure map, China has tagged its blockchain bid at the center, with plans to roll out a nationwide network by 2030. The goal appears in the country’s 15th Five-Year Plan for National Informatization, released by the Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission on October 23.

  • China Sets 2030 Target for National Blockchain Infrastructure
  • Blockchain Expands Beyond a Single National Network
    • China Keeps Crypto Ban While Backing Blockchain
    • National Blockchain Network Becomes Part of China’s Digital Stack

China Sets 2030 Target for National Blockchain Infrastructure

China’s goal is to make significant strides toward informatization by 2030, finishing the rollout of next-generation communications infrastructure and essentially building a national blockchain network, according to the plan. In addition to 6G, AI, and other technologies, Blockchain is also part of Beijing’s bid to upgrade digital infrastructure and implement intelligent internet systems.

The policy also urges China to enhance its own technological landscape and foster globally competitive products in fields such as integrated circuits, new displays, blockchain technology and artificial intelligence.

Technical standards are also a priority. Chinese officials stated that the country will enhance standards in areas such as blockchain, operating systems, databases, and other basic digital technologies.

Read More: ZachXBT Says Chinese Crime Ring Laundered $1B+ for Lazarus After $1.5B Bybit Hack

Blockchain Expands Beyond a Single National Network

But it’s not just about building a single blockchain infrastructure layer. According to the official, blockchain is integrated into the application infrastructure, and a national computing network and smart network development are included. It also links blockchain deployment to broader industrial digitization and data-driven economic activity.

This means that the 2030 target is wider, encompassing a blockchain project as well. Beijing is using distributed-ledger technology to support enterprise, public-sector and industrial applications, not simply run open cryptocurrency markets, with the solution being infrastructure rather than a competitor to cryptocurrencies.

China Keeps Crypto Ban While Backing Blockchain

The new blockchain target is no sign of a reopening of China’s crypto market on the mainland. In February 2026, Chinese financial authorities reiterated once again that activities in virtual currencies are illegal financial activities. The policy applies to services relating to cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether and stablecoins as well as to the oversight of unauthorised real-world asset tokenization.

It’s the pivot of China’s approach: blockchain is welcomed, but the decentralized crypto trading environment is not. The 2026 regulations include a ban on financial institutions that provide services to virtual-currency businesses, and a lingering limit on crypto-mining.

Read More: Poolin, Once-Dominant Bitcoin Mining Giant, Announced Bankruptcy

National Blockchain Network Becomes Part of China’s Digital Stack

Blockchain 2030 is one component in a national strategy that also covers 6G, computing systems, AI systems, and enhanced cybersecurity measures.

According to the official plan, there are 10 key task areas for China, related to infrastructure, the innovation of technology, digital industries, governing, regional coordination, security, technical standards, etc.

The impact on crypto is evident: China is still reinforcing the distinction between permissioned blockchain infrastructure and permissioned applications of tokenized technologies – scaling up the former, also limiting the latter.

title: Ripple Partners With CryptEscrow to Simplify Crypto-Funded U.S. Real Estate Deals

The post Ripple Partners With CryptEscrow to Simplify Crypto-Funded U.S. Real...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Ripple and CryptEscrow to launch regulated foundations for crypto real estate transactions.
  • Sellers and title companies won’t need to take digital coins themselves, but CryptEscrow will manage crypto-to-fiat conversion.
  • It seeks to address the increased demand that crypto investors seek to convert digital assets to property while keeping traditional closing mechanisms.

Ripple is continuing its institutional blockchain progress in real estate with a new partnership with CryptEscrow, a U.S. compliant crypto settlement solution provider.

The collaboration aims to make high-value property purchases easier for buyers holding crypto while keeping traditional closing participants inside familiar fiat-based workflows.

  • Ripple and CryptEscrow Build a Crypto-to-Real Estate Bridge
  • Crypto Holders Can Keep Traditional Closings Intact
    • 67 Million U.S. Crypto Owners Create a Growing Buyer Base
    • Ripple Extends Blockchain Infrastructure Into Real-World Asset Settlement

Ripple and CryptEscrow Build a Crypto-to-Real Estate Bridge

CryptEscrow functional layer between the digital assets and the real estate payments. Instead of requiring sellers, developers, title companies or other parties to handle cryptocurrency directly, buyers can use crypto while settlement proceeds move through regulated fiat channels.

Ripple’s financial infrastructure, available on its blockchain, encompasses payments, custody, treasury operational products and more than that. The partnership will allow for more sizable transactions without compromising compliance, transparency and security during the transaction, CryptEscrow said.

The positioning is the biggest practical hurdle to buyers buying and selling real estate using cryptocurrencies, as it turns digital currency into money that can pass through traditional closing without requiring anyone to use blockchain tools.

Read More: Ripple and Privy Bring XRP Wallets to XRPL After $1T Moved Across 8M Accounts

Crypto Holders Can Keep Traditional Closings Intact

No home seller issues a mandate that they accept Bitcoin, XRP or any other digital asset. CryptEscrow comes the other way round, however, as the controlled agent between the buyer’s crypto assets and the fiat settlement system. That means it’s more about the payment and settlement process than about tokenising the property itself.

This is crucial because the agreement ties cryptocurrency funds to actual assets, rather than overhauling the legal or escrow process currently employed in U.S. real estate transactions.

67 Million U.S. Crypto Owners Create a Growing Buyer Base

The businesses are coming into the market amid an increasing role of crypto in consumers’ spending.

CryptEscrow cited National Cryptocurrency Association data estimating that 67 million Americans own cryptocurrency, roughly one in four adults. It also cited Deloitte research indicating that purchases of homes through crypto increased 35% from the previous year.

Our analysis of a Redfin survey in the press announcement showed that one in 12.7 percent of Gen Z and Millennial homebuyers had already sold cryptocurrency for a down payment. These numbers indicate the expanding number of buyers who can be interested in purchasing belongings with crypto wealth, but may still require regulated banking and escrow platforms, alongside conversion.

Ripple Extends Blockchain Infrastructure Into Real-World Asset Settlement

The real estate partnership joins Ripple’s efforts in regulated financial infrastructure.

Ripple’s institutional offering covers payments, custody, prime brokerage and treasury management services and it has over 85 licenses around the world. Its stablecoin RLUSD and XRP are positioned within that wider infrastructure stack.

title: ECB official sees digital euro as key to protecting EU ‘sovereignty’
summary: Piero Cipollone said the bloc is on track to test real transactions in 2027 and roll out a digital euro as early as 2029, pending legislation this year.
content:
European Central Bank Executive Board member Piero Cipollone said the digital euro that is set for a pilot next year has the potential to give the bloc “sovereignty” over a payments infrastructure that currently requires dependency on external, non-European third parties.

Cipollone said in an interview with Italy’s Milano Finance published by the central bank on Saturday that because the bloc is critically dependent on third parties, it’s not easy to ensure this smooth functioning. He did not cite specific third parties.

“In recent years Europe has learned that, for some essential services, we cannot rely only on third parties. We saw this with energy and we’re seeing it today with defense. And the same is true for payments,” he said.

The pilot will use real transactions by ECB and national central bank staff. With 36 market operators, including seven from Italy, collaborating on preparations, the ECB is inviting e-commerce and mobile-commerce operators to participate.

“The smooth functioning of payment systems is one of our responsibilities. If we are critically dependent on third parties, it’s not easy to ensure this smooth functioning,” Cipollone said.

To be sure, sovereignty doesn’t mean shutting third parties out, Cipollone said. “It means having the power to choose and knowing that, for an essential service like payments, Europe can also rely on its own strength.”

In an April public lecture held in Latvia, Cipollone said that Europe’s reliance on non-European payment providers creates a strategic vulnerability. He said two-thirds of euro-area card transactions are governed by non-European companies, and that the digital euro could reduce that dependence and provide European-controlled payment infrastructure.

The ECB Governing Council can only decide on issuing a digital euro only after legislative negotiations in Brussels conclude. 

“We hope that the regulation will be adopted by the end of the year, enabling the ECB’s Governing Council to issue a formal decision on issuance,” Cipollone told Milano Finance .

  • One episode, a spurious promotion for a ‘fake trade,’ is under scrutiny by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
  • The change follows a week of red flags from Polymarket as it raised $1 billion, valuing itself at $21 billion.

Polymarket reportedly has shed one of its early top executives as the crypto prediction market looks to step out of the startup marketing playbook. According to the New York Post citing sources, Matthew Modabber, the chief marketing officer since January 2024, was fired in the wake of an internal investigation.

  • Polymarket CMO Exit Follows Marketing Controversies
  • Modabber Helped Drive Polymarket’s Explosive Growth
    • $21 Billion Valuation Raises the Stakes
    • Prediction Market Scrutiny Keeps Building

Polymarket CMO Exit Follows Marketing Controversies

Modabber is a company that we saw calling out on some promotional methods, such as staged videos that suggested a user could make money through such trades as didn’t actually exist.

Polymarket earlier stated it would be maintaining accurate, fair and transparent markets and would be considering its promotional material. The internal review also examined reports that influencers were paid through a personal PayPal account, sometimes without clear sponsorship disclosures, according to the New York Post.

Read More: Polymarket Perps Beta Goes Live for 24/7 Trading

Modabber Helped Drive Polymarket’s Explosive Growth

On Linkedin, Modabber identified himself as Polymarket’s 11th employee, and claimed to have launched a marketing, growth and partnerships program that has since grown to include over 50 individuals and brought daily volume from around $300,000 to the mid-nines.

His long tenure with the CEO Shayne Coplan is said to have made the choice a difficult one. The two were acquainted in high school and according to sources, Coplan had resisted attempts to oust him prior to finally agreeing to part ways. Neither Coplan nor Modabber publicly commented on the report.

$21 Billion Valuation Raises the Stakes

The move will mark a change in leadership for Polymarket in critical times. In August, the blockchain-based prediction market raised $1 billion in a funding round led by 1789 Capital, giving the company a $21 billion post-money valuation.

That valuation comes with increased expectations of a large financial platform to operate with compliance, financial controls and governance, as opposed to that of an early stage crypto start-up.

This week Bloomberg also broke news that investors such as Founders Fund had previously urged Polymarket to increase financial checks as it grew.

Prediction Market Scrutiny Keeps Building

The rapid pace of growth has brought crypto prediction markets more under the spotlight. Legislators have raised concerns about practices and potential insider trading in both event-betting clubs and the CFTC is monitoring the sector.

Kalshi has also been seeing greater competition from Polymarket, both of them vying to grab main-stream demand for event contracts. For Polymarket, Modabber’s reported exit signals a shift toward tighter oversight just as the company is trying to turn massive crypto-driven growth into a more mature financial-market business.

title: Latvia targets tokenization rules in 2027 with commercial property in focus
summary: Economics Minister Viktors Valainis says rules could arrive in the first half of next year, but an overdue assessment remains unfinished and no sovereign-bond issuance was identified.
content:
Oct 25, 2026, 11:00 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Latvia could have rules for tokenizing real-world assets in the first half of 2027, with commercial property a possible start, its economics minister said.
  • Government bonds are on the “priority list” and could be tokenized in the first part of next year, Viktors Valainis said, without giving issuance details.
  • A legal assessment due Oct. 1 is “still ongoing,” and Valainis’s party won no seats in this month’s election as Latvia forms a new government.

Latvia could have rules for tokenizing real-world assets in place in the first half of 2027, with commercial property as a possible starting point and government bonds on the list as well.

In an interview with CoinDesk, Economics Minister Viktors Valainis said he expected the work to remain on the agenda of the next government as Latvia forms a new administration.

His ministry is working with the central bank, the Finance Ministry and industry representatives on a framework intended to attract investment.

“If everything goes smoothly, I think next year, first half of the next year, we will already have the regulation,” he said, referring to proposed rules for tokenizing real-world assets, in the interview at the sidelines of UN:BLOCK, a fintech conference in Riga.

He also hopes to promote new products and opportunities linked to the cryptocurrency industry early in 2027.

The work has already passed one deadline. Item 20.5 of the government’s action plan gave the Economics Ministry until Oct. 1 to prepare an assessment of legal changes that would enable the tokenization of real estate and other assets. Asked whether it was complete, Valainis said it was “still ongoing.”

Real estate and bonds

Tokenization creates blockchain-based representations of assets or rights to them. Asked where Latvia would begin, Valainis said commercial property would be a “good start,” but also mentioned the potential use of cryptocurrency to buy or sell companies or invest in property, without going into further detail.

Anti-money-laundering controls remain a central concern, he said, describing a need to understand and manage risks before introducing new rules.

“We don’t want to create something with a big boom and then with a big collapse,” Valainis said. The government will implement solutions only when it is “1,000% sure” they would be transparent and understandable, he added.

Members of the Latvian Blockchain Association (LBAA), which aims to make the country a major Web3 hub in the European Union, participate in working groups and testing, according to the minister.

He named no individual commercial partners, though the LBAA’s members include crypto exchanges like Kraken and Backpack EU, as well as fintech firms like Indemo, Capitalia and Twino, and even the airline airBaltic.

Valainis also said the potential economic benefit had not been quantified, but noted his case for the changes rests on attracting international businesses, investment and tax revenue.

Tokenizing Latvian government bonds is also on the “priority list,” he said. Asked how long it would take to tokenize Latvia’s bonds and real estate once the rules were in place, he said: “I would like to say the first part of the next year. It could be done.”

The Treasury and the ministry’s press office have not answered questions CoinDesk sent on the tokenization efforts.

Other European governments have already tested the technology. Slovenia issued a 30 million euro digital sovereign bond in July 2024, as part of a European Central Bank experiment.

Beyond tokenization

Latvia’s broader ambitions were outlined in May 2025. Valainis said about 40 companies were seeking licenses under the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) framework, and cited approvals within a month.

The country's crypto push also includes allowing personal taxes to be paid with crypto.

“We are at the moment working for the first decision to make it happen,” Valainis said, adding that details such as conversion into euros would follow.

Separately, he reiterated his personal support for a small national crypto reserve, without identifying an approved proposal or purchase timetable.

He renewed his call for a national bitcoin reserve during the interview, saying even a small initial holding would show Latvia was moving toward one.

“There is no way that it won’t happen. It will happen,” he said. He favored “some amount which simply shows that you are doing this step,” pointing to examples in the U.S., including companies that have bought bitcoin.

He said a first step should involve “some common decision together” at the European Central Bank level, but added: “I would be the one who would support faster steps.”

title: UK banks face 10,000 complaints in 3 months over crypto restrictions
summary: The U.K. claims to aspire to become a global cryptocurrency hub, an ambition that would appear to be at odds with the attitude to crypto purchases of its major banks.
content:
Oct 25, 2026, 9:00 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • More than 10,000 complaints about bank restrictions on cryptocurrency transactions were submitted across the U.K. during a 90-day period, according to the advocacy group Stand With Crypto.
  • Lloyds Banking Group received the most complaints, followed by Barclays and NatWest, though the voluntary data was not adjusted for each bank’s market share and does not represent all customers.
  • Stand With Crypto said banks’ blanket bans, rigid limits and unclear policies could impede access to regulated exchanges and undermine Britain’s ambition to become a global cryptocurrency hub.

The U.K.’s desire to become a global cryptocurrency hub appears to have collided with a barrier in the form of the country’s high-street banks.

More than 10,000 complaints about banking restrictions on crypto purchases were submitted by consumers over 90 days between May and August, according to advocacy group Stand With Crypto (SWC).

The country first announced its support for the industry back in 2023, when Rishi Sunak, later prime minister, was still chancellor of the exchequer for the Conservative government. That stance was reiterated by the economic secretary to the Treasury, Lucy Rigby, less than year ago under a Labour administration.

“A country cannot credibly invite innovators in while allowing banks to lock consumers out,” Katie Harries, Coinbase's head of European policy, said in an email interview. “This will undoubtedly dampen the growth of the U.K.’s digital asset sector, with ramifications for associate investment here.”

The 10,092 complaints submitted using an online tool by 9,800 individuals covered customers in all 650 parliamentary constituencies of the U.K., the SWC report said in a report.

Increased friction

The findings expose a potential contradiction in the U.K.’s approach to digital assets. While the government and Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) are preparing a comprehensive regulatory regime intended to attract crypto businesses, banking restrictions can prevent consumers from accessing even regulated venues.

"Bank transfers represent a crucial on-ramp to add money to their account on our platform," said Harries. “We are an FCA-registered crypto asset business, but are subject to the same blanket restrictions as the wider crypto asset sector."

Lloyds Banking Group, which includes Halifax and Bank of Scotland, received the most complaints with 2,297, equivalent to 23% of the total. Barclays followed with 1,569, while NatWest Group received 1,278.

The figures require some qualification. SWC collected complaints from individuals choosing to use its online tool. The poll is not a representative survey of banking customers and is not adjusted for each bank’s share of U.K. checking accounts.

As such, higher figures do not necessarily reflect a higher rate of complaints.

Harries cited research by the U.K. Cryptoasset Business Council indicating that 40% of attempted transfers to FCA-registered crypto exchanges were blocked or delayed during the preceding 12 months.

“Most exchanges said customer friction had increased, and 70% said banking conditions were more hostile than a year earlier,” she said.

Disconnect

Perhaps the report’s most revealing finding, however, is the disconnect between banks’ publicly stated restrictions and what customers say they experience.

Lloyds has no published policy restricting crypto-related transfers, according to SWC’s review of bank websites as of Aug. 28.

Revolut, a digital bank that allows crypto purchases through its app, nevertheless featured among institutions receiving complaints.

Some banks do state explicit limits. Barclays restricts crypto transfers to 2,500 pounds ($3,340) per transaction and 10,000 pounds over 30 days. NatWest and Santander also state transaction and monthly limits. Lenders including Chase, Starling, TSB, Metro Bank and Virgin Money were identified as prohibiting crypto transactions altogether.

Banks with published limits accounted for 61% of the complaints, compared with 28% involving institutions without published restrictions and just under 10% involving banks with outright bans.

SWC argues that the differences raise questions about financial firms’ requirements to provide customers with clear information. A customer looking to switch banks to obtain reliable access to crypto transactions may struggle to determine which institution will actually do what they expect.

Banks have legitimate reasons to scrutinize crypto transfers given the risk of fraud, scams and money laundering.

However, the SWC argues, blanket restrictions go beyond proportionate risk management and conflict with expectations that financial crime controls should assess individual customers and transactions.

SWC proposes banks publishing clear explanations of their restrictions to provide meaningful ways for customers to challenge blocked transfers.

“Banks shouldn’t be allowed to apply blanket restrictions across a whole industry,” Harries said. “They should take a case-by-case approach, not choke off the entire sector.”

title: Netanyahu floats use of blockchain as solution to potential financial sanctions
summary: Ahead of elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel could turn to blockchain and crypto to skirt potential international sanctions, to the dismay of opponents and the country’s central banker.
content:
Blockchain has become an issue in this week’s Israeli elections after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday that the country could turn to cryptocurrency to avoid strains on the economy from any potential international financial sanctions.

He told a local television interviewer that Israel is exploring the use of blockchain technology and cryptocurrencies as a means of circumventing potential banking sanctions.

“Blockchain is an alternative to sanctions,” the prime minister said in an interview with Israel’s Channel 10 economic network on Friday.

His calling blockchain a “national strategic tool” signals a pivot in the government’s stance on the digital currency industry, from an investment event into part of the country’s economic defense strategy, reported CryptoJungle, Israel’s largest crypto media platform.

A dozen Western countries have announced sanctions targeting goods from Israeli settlements in the West Bank in response to Jewish settler attacks on Palestinians and an increase in settlement construction approved by Netanyahu’s right-wing government. Those sanctions could extend into Israel proper, economists and industry figures told The Times of Israel last month.

Several of the candidates seeking to replace Netanyahu in the Oct. 27 elections, as well as the head of the Bank of Israel, were quick to challenge the prime minister’s statement.

“The BibiCoin vision is a threat to national security,” wrote Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot in a Saturday morning X post, using a play on Netanyahu’s nickname. The Bank of Israel in a statement rejected Netanyahu’s proposition, saying that cryptocurrencies “cannot be used as a route for bypassing sanctions.”

Recommended: MoonPay buys crypto security firm Sodot in $100M push into institutional crypto

Sharp reaction on the street and in the media

At Saturday evening’s anti-government rally in Tel Aviv, several onlookers weighed in on Netanyahu’s blockchain statement.

“An economy that runs on the dark web makes us no better than our enemies,” said Aryeh Cohen, holding a sign that said in English “enough Bibi’s B.S.” Another rally attendee who gave only her first name, Pnina, told Cointelegraph “what’s next, the Bank of Israel living ‘neath the law.”

Media critics also lambasted the idea of use of crypto to skirt sanctions.

“The crypto element deserves particular scrutiny. Digital currencies can indeed move value outside some traditional banking channels,” wrote Yediot Ahronot columnist Nadav Eyal in an X post. “But they are not a substitute for a national financial system. They don’t provide credit lines to banks, they don’t replace international capital markets, and they don’t persuade foreign companies to violate sanctions that bar them from doing business with Israel.”

“Crypto & blockchain-based solutions are not the tool for bypassing sanctions,” Ben Samocha, founder of CryptoJungle, told Cointelegraph on Sunday. “As demonstrated by the US Treasury against Iran, blockchain investigation allows tracking illicit funds, blocking their fiat gateway, and even freezing them.” He said that the Israeli economy is not fit to bypass sanctions using crypto.

Traders are looking to test the lows as the momentum slows and major support levels present themselves, and then whether the selling pressure will persist or turn to a rally before the end of December.

The swift drop in silver prices in October has put the precious metal at a pivotal level, and the metal has dropped by almost 6% over the last week.

Silver Extends Its October Decline as Selling Pressure Builds

The supplied Trading Economics chart shows silver prices dropping 5.96% for the week to $53.883 per ounce.The weekly chang show-3.412. The prices were again hovering around $53.9 on October 24, and the chart was indicating a big pullback from above $57 earlier this week.

The drop further escalated since October 22, when silver breached the $56 level and headed down to $54. Source: TradingEconomics

The price closed in the mid-$50s, before stabilising a fraction of a penny higher. The chart displays a brief period of consolidation late in the week; however, this is not yet a confirmation of a longer-term reversal.

Further market commentary also highlights yield pressures, a stronger US dollar and interest-rate expectations. On October 23, FOREX.com news agency said that silver had found a long-term support base of 50-55 after a wide precious-metals sell-off.

TradingView Signals Point to a Weak Technical Structure

As of October 24, silver was trading at $53.918 on the provided TradingView chart, which had declined by 1.26% during the session. The displayed moving averages were at $61.309 and $63.618, respectively, which were still above the price. Both were on a downward trend, suggesting that prices in recent times have been subdued during the considered time periods.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) was at 31.58, which is below the average level of 38.21. The latest reading puts silver near the 30 level, which is typically seen as oversold. Source: TradingView

But this isn’t a conclusive sign of recovery, especially if the prices continue in the form of lower lows. The first important area of the technical zone is the interval between $53 and $55. Any continuation of the trend below $53 would leave the market open for more losses to the $50 price level.

On the other hand, a recovery above $55 will signal an initial stabilisation. However, with more evidence of a change in trend, silver would need to reach higher levels and test resistance at $61-$64.

These levels are technical levels that you are given in this chart and NOT guaranteed future trading levels. A change in the price action may be in sight, depending on the direction of US Treasury yields, the dollar and the general sentiment on precious metals.

October and December Forecasts rely on a Market Reversal.

October and December Forecasts Depend on a Market Reversal

However, the charts are looking for caution for the rest of the month as silver is still trading below its period averages. A break above $55 would signal a short-term recovery, while a drop below $53 would increase downside risk. The 50-55 zone continues to be significant as market analysts have found it to be a wider support area.

December is a more ambiguous month. In the August forecast, J.P. Morgan had an average of $63/oz. for Q4 and $70.60/oz. for 2026. The forecast aligned with expectations of easing physical-market tightness, declining industrial demand, and interest-rate pressures. These are average which are forecasts and do not guarantee December closing prices.

On X, Rashad Hajiyev stated that silver has formed a long-term cup and handle breakout and retest. Prices may even reach $200 by 2027, he said. Source: X Via Rashad

This, of course, is an analyst’s bull case and not a market consensus or actual projection. Buyers would have needed to take control and break out of the technical resistance near $60–$63 to make a move in December.

A continued lacklustre performance may instead drag silver down to around $50–$55. The evidence provided herein suggests that the next few months are a period of caution until prices recover and cross key moving averages, but the longer-term trend depends on monetary policy, industrial demand and investment flows.

title: Strategy, Strive face balancing act between bitcoin buying and preferred stock dividends
summary: The securities have financed purchases of nearly 136,000 bitcoin, opening a funding channel that analysts expect to complement the larger ETF market.
content:
Oct 24, 2026, 12:00 p.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Since 2025, preferred stocks funded purchases of 135,979 BTC through Oct. 5, Fidelity said.
  • Bitwise expects ETFs to remain the larger demand source, with preferreds attracting yield investors.
  • Dividend obligations and buybacks could constrain further bitcoin purchases.

Bitcoin BTC$84,459.46 treasury companies like Strategy (MSTR) and Strive (ASST), whose purchases help maintain demand for the largest cryptocurrency, have a tough balancing act, according to Fidelity Digital Assets and analysts who spoke to CoinDesk.

On the one hand, they need cash to fund their purchases. On the other, they need to maintain investor appetite for new sales of the perpetual preferred stock that is their favored fundraising vehicle. As the number of shares in circulation grows, so do the dividend payments.

The securities, which sit between debt and common equity in the capital structure with regular payouts and no voting rights, have financed purchases of some 136,000 bitcoin in the 20 months since their introduction, Fidelity research analyst Zack Wainwright wrote in a Tuesday report. That’s more than 0.5% of the cryptocurrency’s maximum supply.

Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder, is the dominant company in the market. Its preferred shares — it has five different classes — make it a bellwether for the model’s durability. Its first offering, STRK, debuted in February 2025.

Fidelity puts the bitcoin-focused preferred market at roughly $12 billion. The global fixed-income market is $150 trillion, suggesting there’s room for growth.

Reaching yield investors

By selling preferred shares that offer dividends without a fixed maturity, the companies reduce refinancing pressure while attracting investors reluctant to own bitcoin directly.

“Perpetual preferreds have brought bitcoin to income investors, a group that ETFs never reached,” said Mark Palmer, a senior equity research analyst at StoneX.

Ryan Rasmussen, the head of research at Bitwise, also sees the products attracting buyers who might avoid bitcoin exchange-traded funds, though he expects the ETFs to remain the bigger demand channel.

“Over the long run, I expect ETFs to be a larger source of demand for bitcoin, with perpetual preferred offerings acting as a second tailwind addressing a different type of investor (yield investors),” Rasmussen said.

James Butterfill, CoinShares’ head of research, said STRC alone, which pays a variable dividend currently around 12%, raised $7.5 billion during 2026 through late July. That funding carries a recurring dividend cost.

Alex Blume, the founder and CEO of institutional bitcoin asset manager Two Prime, pointed out that products such as STRC and Strive’s SATA don’t offer just exposure to bitcoin prices. Their price also reacts to management competence, issuers’ obligations and capital-market conditions.

He cited STRC briefly falling into the $70 range in late June as evidence of potential volatility. Growing issuance creates a tension between increasing bitcoin per common share, meeting dollar-denominated dividend-payout commitments and avoiding bitcoin sales, he said. The Strategy preferred stock currently trades around $99.40.

Buybacks compete with purchases

“The catch is that the demand for perpetual preferreds is reflexive,” Palmer said. Continued preferred-funded buying depends on the securities trading at or near par, he added. Below par, fresh issuance becomes less attractive, and companies may favor repurchases, Butterfill said.

Strategy’s latest weekly update reported $193 million spent repurchasing STRC alongside purchases of just 267 bitcoin, according to Butterfill. The firm also increased its preferred-stock repurchase authorization to $3 billion, he said.

“Buybacks can reduce future dividend costs, but they compete with bitcoin purchases for capital today,” Butterfill said.

Cash reserves provide a buffer, although Strategy has already sold some bitcoin to fund preferred dividends, he added.

ETFs remain the larger channel

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs have attracted approximately $57 billion in cumulative net inflows and hold around $106 billion in assets, Butterfill said.

Net ETF creations increase funds’ bitcoin holdings, while issuance of preferred stock gives management discretion over spending. Redemptions can reverse ETF demand but leave no continuing dividend commitment, he said.

Butterfill sees preferreds amplifying the cycle: supporting purchases when financing conditions are favorable, with that support weakening as sentiment deteriorates.

title: Block's new voice AI sounds eerily human, sparking awe and scam fears
summary: Reactions split between amazement at how human it sounds and fears it could fuel scams and deception, with CZ eyeing uses in children’s education.
content:
Oct 24, 2026, 11:21 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Block unveiled Dessa, a voice AI trained only on human speech that talks without text and runs locally on a MacBook Pro with an M4 Max chip.
  • Reactions split between amazement at how human it sounds and fears it could fuel scams and deception, with CZ eyeing uses in children’s education.
  • Block hasn’t disclosed model size, benchmarks or a release date; the research preview is going first to a small group of AI safety researchers.

Jack Dorsey's payments company Block XYZ$76.45·Market Closed has unveiled a voice AI model that sounds remarkably human in company demonstrations, prompting reactions ranging from amazement at its conversational abilities to warnings that such technology could make phone scams harder to detect.

Called Dessa, the model was trained entirely on human speech rather than text and can listen while speaking, allowing it to handle interruptions, laughter and changes in tone during a conversation, according to the Block’s announcement.

“Talking with it feels like talking with a person…full of emotion, nuance, pauses, and a natural cadence,” Dorsey wrote on X.

In one demonstration, Dessa laughs in the middle of a sentence; in another, it reacts to a surprise with what sounds like genuine emotion. Block says the conversations were recorded live without anyone directing the model's responses.

Unlike systems that first convert speech into text before generating a spoken response, Dessa processes audio directly. Block said it trained Dessa from scratch using a single Nvidia GB200 NVL72 computing system. The model is compact enough to run locally on a MacBook Pro equipped with an M4 Max chip or better, according to the firm’s statement.

For now, Dessa remains a research preview rather than a publicly available product.

Shock and awe

Dessa’s demo quickly drew attention on social media, with some users praising how natural the interactions sounded.

X user Alexander Hoff said he had never “heard anything artificial that sounded so… human,” while user Hesamation described it as “straight up sci-fi stuff.

Binance founder Changpeng “CZ” Zhao also chimed in, pointing to potential uses in education, where natural voice interactions could help children learn through conversation.

“This might be very good for GiggleAcademy. Teaching kids in current ‘AI voice’ was a challenge,” Zhao wrote, referring to his education project.

But the same humanlike qualities that impressed some listeners raised concerns among others about the technology's potential for deception.

Filmmaker Justine Bateman questioned why AI voices need to sound human, arguing that it could be used to mislead people. “So you can trick people into lowering their guard,” she wrote.

Journalist Shiv Aroor raised similar concerns about fraud, writing, “Scam calls about to attain pandemic level.”

Dessa comes from Block, which operates Square, Cash App, bitcoin wallet Bitkey and bitcoin mining hardware unit Proto. Its AI research lab reports directly to Dorsey and includes former staff from Toronto-based AI startup Dessa, which Square acquired in 2020.

Block has not disclosed the model’s size, benchmark results or a public release date. Its audio samples remain company demonstrations rather than independent tests.

The company is offering early access to a small group of AI safety researchers. Block says speech-based AI could eventually become better at recognizing emotional cues, such as distress and pain, that text transcripts can miss, while researchers assess risks the company may have overlooked.

title: Why McDonalds, Microsoft and Google saying no to tokenized stocks isn't a dealbreaker
summary: Some of the world's biggest companies objected to being listed on the first tokenized securities trading venue under the SEC's innovation exemption. But the early pushback may say more about issuer caution than about rejection of tokenization itself.
content:
4 мин чтения

Кратко

This is an excerpt from CoinDesk's new ‘Tokenization Weekly’ newsletter that will be launching soon. Sign-up details will be here when it goes live.

The SEC's new framework for tokenized stock trading looked, at first glance, roughly a month ago, like a fast track to putting U.S. equities on crypto rails.

The first real-world test hasn't looked particularly encouraging so far.

A growing group of public companies has objected to having their shares traded on the tokenized-securities venue being built by OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the owner of the New York Stock Exchange.

This week’s of objections included some of the biggest names yet: Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), Goldman Sachs (GS) McDonalds (MCD) and three others on Monday, then Wells Fargo (WFC) and Cisco (CSCO) and four more firms on Friday rejected having tokenized versions of their shares traded on OKXICE, bringing the disclosed total now to 22 objecting issuers.

Seeing some of the world's largest companies say no may not exactly be the start that tokenization advocates had hoped for.

But it also isn't necessarily a major blow to the SEC's experiment.

Read more: OKX-ICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo calls corporate objections a ‘natural response’ to tokenized stock plans

Why it matters

Before trading in a company's shares, a venue must notify the issuer and give the issuer 30 days to object. If the company stays silent, trading can begin.

That gives public companies a say in whether unaffiliated third parties tokenize and trade their shares, but it also tilts the decision toward caution.

Global law firm Latham & Watkins has warned issuers that silence effectively becomes an irrevocable decision: the SEC order provides no mechanism to object after the 30-day window or withdraw a prior non-objection once trading begins.

So when a legal or investor-relations team receives notice about a new market structure it may know little about, saying no while it figures things out can be the rational choice.

“Most of these companies had no idea a third party had tokenized their stock until the OKXICE notice went up,” Dave Hendricks, CEO and founder of tokenization firm Vertalo, told CoinDesk.

“Once they do, the questions come fast: who holds the shares behind the token, how do dividends and votes reach those holders, what does the transfer agent see?” he added.

If those questions can't be answered within 30 days, he said, objecting makes sense.

Olivia Vande Woude, head of tokenization at Ava Labs, also cautioned against reading the growing list as a verdict on OKXICE.

“It's the first venue to send notices under the SEC's Innovation Exemption, so it's the first to get the answers,” she said.

And because objecting costs nothing while silence counts as consent, she expects the list to keep growing.

“Given how easy the opt-out is, the list of objectors is likely to keep growing, and the next venue that sends notices should expect similar resistance,” Vande Woude said.

That may be less a sign that the experiment is failing than an indication of what the experiment is uncovering.

“This exemption is a data-gathering exercise,” Vande Woude said. “What it's showing is that public companies want a say in how their shares come onchain.”

What comes next

Nasdaq offers a useful example of what the objections do – and don't – mean.

The exchange operator has been a vocal supporter of tokenization and is pursuing its own model for tokenized securities. But Nasdaq Inc., whose shares trade under NDAQ, said it intends to object to having tokenized versions of its own stock traded on TSVs under the current exemption.

That reflects a disagreement over market structure, not tokenization itself.

Nasdaq warned that TSVs operating outside the National Market System (NMS) could fragment liquidity, weaken price discovery and lack safeguards such as real-time best-price display and consolidated-tape reporting. Its own model keeps tokenized securities inside the existing exchange framework.

There is also a simpler question for issuers: what's in it for them?

Reid Noch, vice president of U.S. equity market structure at TD Securities, told CoinDesk the bigger issue is that the upside for issuers remains difficult to quantify. Tokenization could bring additional demand for U.S. shares, particularly from overseas investors, but the SEC framework may not generate enough new demand to offset the risks of thin, 24/7 trading outside the familiar market structure.

That doesn't mean everyone is saying no.

Securitize (SECZ), which specializes in tokenized securities, told CoinDesk it does not plan to object to inclusion on the OKX-ICE venue. A representative of digital asset custodian BitGo (BTGO) also said in an email that the company won't object to the listing.

Both have an obvious interest in helping the tokenized-asset market grow, but Securitize's response also pointed to what may be needed for more traditional companies to get comfortable.

“There's an important education process underway,” CEO Carlos Domingo said.

The firm said it has been reaching out to issuers that are or may become involved with its own tokenized stocks, including through webinars explaining the different trading models, shareholder rights and potential trade-offs.

That probably offers the clearest glimpse of what comes next: Education and time.

The SEC may have removed one regulatory barrier to tokenized stock trading. Getting public companies comfortable enough to use it could take considerably longer.

title: Argentina drops criminal probe into President Milei over crashed memecoin LIBRA
summary: The judge found that Milei's promotion of LIBRA did not constitute fraud, despite the attention his support drew to the token.
content:
Oct 24, 2026, 10:38 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • An Argentine judge dismissed the criminal probe into President Javier Milei, his sister Karina and LIBRA adviser Hayden Davis.
  • The judge found that Milei's promotion of LIBRA did not constitute fraud, despite the attention his support drew to the token.
  • LIBRA lost more than 95% of its value after reaching about $5, while wallets linked to its creator withdrew around $99 million in cryptocurrency.

An Argentine federal judge has dismissed the criminal case against President Javier Milei over his promotion of LIBRA, a memecoin that crashed soon after its launch in February 2025.

The ruling also covers Milei's sister Karina, the presidency's secretary general. U.S. businessman Hayden Davis, who described himself as an adviser to the token's launch, was also covered by the dismissal, Reuters reported.

In all, 11 people were cleared, including lobbyist Mauricio Novelli and KIP Protocol CEO Julian Peh, according to Infobae. None of them had been formally questioned in the case.

Judge Marcelo Martínez de Giorgi acknowledged that Milei's endorsement could have given the launch "greater impact,” but said his social media post and LIBRA's subsequent collapse were insufficient to establish fraud without evidence of a specific deception, the report adds, citing court records.

The judge also found no evidence that Karina Milei sought or received money in exchange for access to the president, or that proceeds from LIBRA reached public officials, according to Argentine fact-checking outlet Chequeado.

In February 2025, CoinDesk reported that it had obtained text messages in which Davis bragged about buying access to the president’s inner circle, sent money to Karina Milei, and claimed he could influence the president's decisions. Davis subsequently denied making any payments to either Milei or his sister.

Milei promoted LIBRA on X on Feb. 14, 2025, saying the Solana-based token would help fund small businesses in Argentina. It rose exponentially before losing more than 90% of its value, leading to the destruction of over $250 million in investor wealth.

Blockchain researchers found that eight wallets linked to the token's creator had withdrawn around $99 million in crypto, according to the report. Davis said he held close to $100 million after the crash but denied wrongdoing.

Milei later deleted his post and denied ties to LIBRA. He said he had acted in good faith and pulled his support after learning more about the project.

In an official statement, the president's office said the judge granted a prosecutor's request to dismiss the case because the acts under review did not constitute a crime. It characterized the probe, opened ahead of Argentina’s 2025 midterm elections, as an attempt to harm Milei’s reputation in an election year.

The case may not be fully closed, however.

Prosecutor Eduardo Taiano, who requested the dismissal, is not expected to appeal. In July, the judge removed the investors who had joined the case as plaintiffs, and an appeals court upheld that decision in September.

Those investors have challenged their removal before the Federal Criminal Cassation Court. If they are reinstated, they could appeal the dismissal.

title: XRP’s Hidden Value Advantage? David Schwartz Drops Bombshell on XRPL Adoption
summary: Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz has outlined why XRP could benefit from broader adoption of the XRP Ledger (XRPL), pointing to its role in transaction processing, liquidity, and asset transfers.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XRP

Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz has outlined why XRP could benefit from broader adoption of the XRP Ledger (XRPL), pointing to its role in transaction processing, liquidity, and asset transfers.

Schwartz’s comments add to the debate over whether XRP’s long-term value depends on speculation or practical demand.

The discussion centered on transaction fees, token burning, and XRP’s function as a bridge asset. Schwartz argues that the token’s built-in advantages could support demand as XRPL expands, although greater network activity does not guarantee a higher market price.

The Core Thesis

Schwartz linked XRPL’s low transaction costs and reliable operation to its potential to attract financial activity, arguing that XRP could capture some of the resulting value.

David Schwartz identifies XRPL autobridging as a mechanism through which XRP’s liquidity-bridge role can drive demand and directly influence its value. Source: X

“Low fees and reliable operation make XRPL a great place to move and hold value,” Schwartz wrote. “That drives value flow to XRPL. XRP captures some of that value because of its unique advantages over other assets on XRPL.”

His explanation distinguishes the usefulness of the ledger from the value of its native token. XRPL can attract transactions through its technical capabilities, while XRP benefits when those activities create demand for its specific functions.

Why XRP Specifically?

XRP has a distinct position on XRPL because it is the network’s native asset. Unlike issued currencies and tokens, it does not require an issuer or a trust line to be held and transferred between accounts.

This makes XRP a potential intermediary for exchanges between different assets. XRPL’s built-in decentralized exchange supports auto-bridging, which can route trades through the token when the combined exchange rates are more favorable than a direct trade.

This functionality gives the token a practical role in connecting markets, although its use depends on available liquidity and competitive trading offers.

Structural Advantages

XRP’s functions extend beyond trading. Network transactions require XRP for fees, while accounts must maintain the token reserves for certain ledger operations. Transaction fees are permanently destroyed, helping protect XRPL against spam, while reserves limit the growth of ledger entries.

These mechanisms establish functional requirements for XRP, but their direct effect on market price remains uncertain. Fees are generally small, and the reserved token is held rather than permanently removed from circulation.

Schwartz’s argument centers on whether these structural advantages translate into sustained demand as financial activity develops on XRPL.

XRPL Success Without High XRP Demand Is Very Unlikely: David Schwartz

Schwartz believes widespread adoption of XRPL for financial applications without meaningful demand for XRP would be unlikely.

“I think a world where XRPL is highly successful in financial applications, but XRP does not have high demand and value is very unlikely,” he said.

Schwartz highlights XRPL autobridging as a direct utility mechanism through which XRP usage can drive price, distinct from indirect effects such as speculation. Source: X

His position reflects XRP’s role in the ledger’s transaction and liquidity infrastructure. However, network adoption and token valuation remain distinct: activity could increase without a comparable rise in the token’s demand if users primarily transact in other assets or hold the token only briefly.

Market prices also depend on liquidity, investor expectations, and broader cryptocurrency conditions.

How XRPL Adoption Will Increase XRP Demand

Schwartz’s thesis identifies two potential demand channels:

  • Transaction fees and account reserves: Users need XRP to pay transaction fees and meet applicable reserve requirements, creating functional demand for the asset.
  • Liquidity and auto-bridging: XRP can connect trading pairs when routing an exchange through the token offers a competitive rate, potentially facilitating transactions between otherwise disconnected markets.

The strength of these channels will depend on actual usage, trading volumes, and liquidity conditions. Their existence demonstrates XRP’s utility but does not establish how much additional demand or price appreciation may result.

Do XRP Burns Increase Its Price?

The community discussion also examined whether permanently destroying transaction fees directly increases XRP’s market value.

XRP supporter Saul argued that the burning mechanism was designed primarily to prevent spam rather than support the token’s price. Excessively high fees could also discourage network use.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Although burning reduces the outstanding supply at the margin, its price impact depends on the amount destroyed relative to available supply and changes in demand. Schwartz’s argument places greater emphasis on XRP’s practical uses than on fee burning alone.

XRP Benefits Even if Bitcoin Dominates

Schwartz also argued that XRP could retain a useful role even if Bitcoin remains the dominant settlement asset in the cryptocurrency market.

The token can facilitate exchanges between different assets on XRPL without becoming the final asset received or the primary store of value. Auto-bridging allows it to connect markets when trading conditions make that route advantageous.

Its potential usefulness therefore does not depend on displacing Bitcoin. However, the extent of XRP’s role will depend on actual liquidity and whether routing trades through the token offers a competitive result.

Vet Highlights XRPL Built-In Exchange

XRPL validator Vet has highlighted the network’s built-in decentralized exchange as another feature supporting its financial infrastructure.

The exchange allows users to trade supported assets through the ledger’s protocol, while auto-bridging can connect separate markets through XRP. The circulation of additional assets, including Ripple USD (RLUSD), could broaden trading opportunities on XRPL.

However, adding tokens does not automatically increase XRP demand. The effect depends on trading activity and whether the token provides an effective route between markets.

The Main Takeaway

Schwartz’s comments present a utility-based case for XRP, emphasizing its role in transaction processing, account reserves, and liquidity provision rather than relying on token burning alone.

XRPL’s auto-bridging mechanism illustrates how XRP can connect markets without becoming the dominant settlement asset. Whether these advantages translate into sustained demand will depend on real-world usage, liquidity, and broader market conditions.

Schwartz’s thesis explains why XRPL adoption could benefit XRP, but the scale of that benefit remains dependent on measurable demand rather than network growth alone.
