title: Wells Fargo, Cisco, Marvell among latest firms objecting to OKXICE's tokenized stock plan
summary: Six more companies have objected to listing tokenized versions of their stock on the venue, Reuters reported, bringing the total to 22.
content:
Oct 24, 2026, 10:06 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Cisco, Wells Fargo, Marvell, Arm, Intuit and Moderna opted out of OKXICE’s plans to offer blockchain-based trading of their tokenized shares, bringing the total number of objections to 22.
  • The growing list highlights a hurdle for the joint venture of the crypto exchange and NYSE parent under the SEC’s new framework, which gives issuers 30 days to block their shares from trading on a tokenized securities venue.
  • OKXICE co-chairman Andrew Cuomo said objections were expected, with many companies preferring to wait and see how the new market works before participating.

Cisco (CSCO), Wells Fargo (WFC) and four other companies have opted out of plans by crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) to offer blockchain-based trading of their shares, bringing the total objections to 22 as issuers weigh participation in the SEC’s new framework for tokenized stocks.

The companies, along with Arm Holdings (ARM), Moderna (MRNA), Intuit (INTU) and Marvell Technology (MRVL), were named in an updated public notice filed Friday by OKXICE, the two firms’ joint venture.

The additions extend a list that already included some of the world’s largest publicly traded companies, such as Microsoft MSFT$524.32·Market Closed, Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), Goldman Sachs (GS) and McDonald’s and said no to the venue’s plan in recent weeks.

The growing number of objections signals a hurdle for a new market structure that would let U.S. investors trade stocks around the clock on blockchains. The SEC’s five-year “Innovation Exemption” allows qualifying tokenized securities venues, or TSVs, to test trading through automated market makers — software that executes trades using pools of assets — while giving issuers a say in whether their shares participate.

OKXICE, backed by one of the world's biggest exchange operators, issued its initial public notice on Oct. 4, outlining plans to use Uniswap (UNI) liquidity pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, with transactions settled in stablecoins. Venues must notify issuers and give them 30 days to object before offering tokenized versions of their shares.

The venture’s original proposed trading roster covered 62 companies. Wells Fargo and ARM were not among them, while Cisco, Moderna, Intuit and Marvell were included.

That means the 22 objections cannot all be counted as departures from the original selection. Cerebras Systems, whose objection was disclosed earlier, was also outside that roster. An objection blocks trading on the notifying venue but does not establish opposition to every form of stock tokenization.

Companies take a wait-and-see approach

Andrew Cuomo, OKXICE’s co-chairman and former New York governor, said earlier this week that such responses were expected.

“We always anticipated that, because this is such a dramatic and revolutionary change, many companies would want to wait and see how it goes rather than be the first to participate,” Cuomo said during a Monday press call.

Limits on participating companies and trading volumes make the framework “a sandbox — a model demonstration,” he said.

title: Ethereum (ETH) Price Prediction: Whale Rotates $155M Into ETH as Longs Surge Near $2,500
summary: Ethereum (ETH) is showing signs of a potential bullish recovery as rising whale activity, growing long positions, and improving technical setups put the next major price move in focus.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ETH

Ethereum (ETH) is showing signs of a potential bullish recovery as rising whale activity, growing long positions, and improving technical setups put the next major price move in focus.

Ethereum is trying to stabilize after another volatile stretch, with price returning toward the mid-$2,400 region while several positioning signals begin to turn more constructive. According to Brave New Coin, ETH is trading around $2,460.98, up 0.52% over the past 24 hours.

Ethereum Sees Short-term Breakout Above $2,415

Ethereum has started recovering from the latest drop, but the lower-timeframe structure still shows unfinished resistance overhead. Crypto Tony’s intraday chart highlights repeated rejection around the recent local high, with price struggling to convert rebound attempts into a clean structural breakout.

The chart places immediate support around the $2,380-$2,370 region, where buyers previously stepped in after the latest decline. Holding above that area would allow ETH price to continue building a base, but the recovery needs to extend through the nearby resistance and ultimately reclaim $2,415 before the short-term trend begins to look materially stronger.

Ethereum price has already produced several rebound attempts during the correction. A move above resistance that quickly fails would leave price vulnerable to another retest lower, whereas sustained acceptance above $2,415 would begin shifting attention back towards $2,500 and the next higher resistance zone.

Ethereum is recovering from recent lows, but the lower-timeframe structure still requires a stronger reclaim above resistance. Source: Crypto Tony via X

Whale Rotates $155 Million Into ETH Near $2,460

Large-holder activity is beginning to strengthen the bullish case around Ethereum. Lookonchain data shared by Cointelegraph shows one whale selling approximately 1,917.7 BTC worth $159 million over the past 11 days while buying 64,545 ETH valued at roughly $155 million.

That rotation puts Ethereum at the center of attention, especially while ETH is trying to stabilize around the $2,400-$2,500 region. The whale is building a sizable position during weakness, which adds to the idea that larger investors are becoming more interested in Ethereum before a stronger recovery is confirmed.

A major whale has rotated roughly $159 million out of Bitcoin while purchasing about $155 million worth of Ethereum. Source: Cointelegraph on X.

If ETH price can now reclaim nearby resistance and begin holding higher, this kind of whale accumulation would add more weight to the recovery narrative. For now, the transaction stands out as one of the stronger demand-side signals developing around Ethereum.

ETH Longs Surge as Shorts Collapse Near $2,460

Ethereum’s derivatives positioning is becoming increasingly bullish as traders reduce short exposure and build long positions around the current range. Data shared by Trader Symba shows ETH shorts falling from above 14,000 to roughly 3,000, while long exposure has climbed from below 100 million to around 365 million.

Ethereum short exposure has dropped sharply while long positioning has expanded toward roughly 365 million. Source: Trader Symba via X

That shift puts more attention on Ethereum’s ability to turn positioning into price strength. Traders are clearly leaning toward the upside before ETH price has fully cleared resistance, which suggests growing confidence that the current base can support another recovery attempt.

If Ethereum begins reclaiming the $2,500 area, the buildup in longs could help strengthen momentum while the reduction in shorts removes some of the pressure that had been weighing on price. Until then, the derivatives market is signaling a much stronger bullish bias than it was earlier in the correction.

Ethereum Price Prediction Targeting $8,800

Ethereum’s longer-term setup places the current market inside what Merlin The Trader identifies as a major accumulation zone between roughly $2,270 and $2,500. Rather than treating the recent weakness as the end of the broader cycle, the roadmap views this range as the area where longer-term positions can begin to build.

The next stage comes around $3,000-$3,300. A recovery into that region would represent an important shift in structure and provide stronger evidence that Ethereum is moving out of accumulation and back into expansion. The plan therefore increases exposure only after price begins confirming the recovery rather than relying on the current base alone.

If that larger trend develops, the roadmap eventually targets the $8,800 region, with the broader distribution zone extending toward approximately $11,500. Those levels remain longer-term objectives, but the sequence makes the present $2,270-$2,500 range particularly important: holding the base and eventually reclaiming $3,000-$3,300 would keep the higher Ethereum price prediction in play.

Source: Merlin The Trader via X.

Ethereum Short-Term Indicators Are Oversold

Ethereum’s short-term indicators have cooled enough to leave more room for a recovery attempt. The 2-hour RSI has fallen back toward 47 after being much stronger earlier, showing that the market has worked off a large part of its previous momentum without dropping into a deeply oversold condition.

The MACD is still negative, but the recent reset means ETH is no longer stretched on the upside. If buying pressure starts to return, both RSI and MACD now have more space to turn higher alongside price, which could support another recovery move from the current area.

Looking Ahead: What Traders Should Watch Next

The next move will likely depend on whether Ethereum can turn the current stabilization into a stronger reclaim. The first level to watch is the $2,400 area, which is where price is trying to base again. If that zone continues to hold, traders will likely start looking back toward $2,455 and then the recent recovery high near $2,500, where the last upside attempt ran into trouble.

If buyers can reclaim $2,500, the structure starts to improve and the conversation can shift back toward higher resistance levels. If not, and ETH price loses the $2,370-$2,400 support band, then the recent recovery starts to look more like another temporary bounce inside a weaker range. In that case, traders would likely turn their focus back toward the lower support pocket around $2,345.

title: Weekly Review: IG Seeks UK Gambling Licence; Plus500 to Acquire Brazilian Broker
summary:
The retail trading industry saw developments across
regulation, market access, acquisitions and customer acquisition this week. IG
Group moved closer to offering prediction markets in the UK, while Plus500
agreed to buy a Brazilian broker as it continued expanding its multi-asset
business. 
Google a...
content:
2026-10-24T09:00:00.000+02:00

Saturday, 24/10/2026 | 07:00 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Capital.com UAE clients traded $1.1 trillion, but only 18.3% of trades had stop-losses set.
  • Google lifts its Danish ban on CFD and forex ads and allows them in Chile for authorised advertisers.

The retail trading industry saw developments across regulation, market access, acquisitions and customer acquisition this week. IG Group moved closer to offering prediction markets in the UK, while Plus500 agreed to buy a Brazilian broker as it continued expanding its multi-asset business.

Google also revised its advertising policy for contracts for difference in two markets, potentially reopening access to paid search campaigns for eligible providers.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Elsewhere, salary data highlighted differences between financial centres, while Capital.com’s trading figures offered insight into client behaviour. Prop trading, institutional access to prediction markets and the economics of broker marketing also featured in the week’s developments.

In digital assets, new figures highlighted the gap between the growth of tokenised real-world asset ownership and the trading activity needed to support liquid secondary markets.

Dubai Compliance Chiefs Earn Up to $425K as Cyprus FX Salaries Rise 14%

FinTop Consulting’s 2026 salary surveys showed substantial differences in compensation across Dubai, London and Cyprus. Dubai-based Chief Compliance Officers can earn between $310,000 and $425,000 annually, with the lower benchmark matching the upper salary benchmark for Chief Technology Officers.

London Heads of Compliance can earn up to $251,000, while regulatory specialists handling additional responsibilities command premiums of 10% to 20%.

Cyprus recorded annual salary growth of 14% across its foreign exchange and fintech sectors, compared with approximately 4% across UAE financial services. The figures point to differing compensation trends across the three financial centres.

Dubai’s compliance salaries also exceed those available for several commercial executive roles, although some technology and risk positions can command higher maximum pay.

IG Applies for UK Gambling Licence to Offer Prediction Markets

IG Group has applied for a UK gambling licence to offer prediction markets covering sports, politics and entertainment, with a launch planned for early 2027.

The application was submitted through its London subsidiary, IG View Limited, which appears on the Gambling Commission’s register under the trading name ig prediction markets.

The application remains pending, and the licence has not been granted.

The company also plans to introduce financial event contracts for UK professional clients in the fourth quarter of 2026. Its expansion follows an agreement to acquire US fantasy sports and prediction markets operator Underdog for up to approximately $1.3 billion.

The deal is expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027. IG’s plans would extend its offering beyond conventional leveraged trading products.

Capital.com UAE Clients Trade $1 Trillion

Capital.com clients in the United Arab Emirates traded $1.06 trillion during the first half of 2026, accounting for more than two-fifths of the broker’s $2.45 trillion in total trading volume.

UAE trading volume increased 27.7% from the second half of 2025, while closed trades rose 48% to 80.9 million, according to the broker’s H1 2026 Pulse Report.

However, only 18.3% of UAE trades had a stop-loss set, the lowest proportion among seven markets covered. Germany recorded the highest rate at 34.1%, followed by the Netherlands at 32.8%.

Across Capital.com, 22.4% of closed trades carried a stop-loss set at entry. The report also found that positions closed after a stop-loss trigger recorded 39% lower average losses, although it described this as a correlation rather than proof of causation.

Hantec Trader Rebrands as RZR Funded

Hantec Trader, the proprietary trading business within the Hantec Group, has rebranded as RZR Funded and changed the name of its operating company from Hantec Trader Limited to RZR Funded Limited. The firm said the change establishes a separate identity for its prop trading operations as it prepares for further development.

The business remains part of the Hantec Group and continues to be powered by Hantec Markets Mauritius, the group’s retail broker arm regulated by the Financial Services Commission.

RZR Funded Director Bashaar Gokal said the company was expanding its executive team and preparing to introduce new asset classes and trading tools. He added that existing traders should not expect immediate operational changes as a result of the rebrand.

Google Reopens CFD Advertising in Denmark and Chile

Google has updated its policy on complex speculative financial products to permit advertising for CFDs, rolling spot forex and similar products in Denmark and Chile. The changes take effect in October, although Google has not specified an exact date.

Advertisers in Denmark must hold the relevant authorisation from the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority, while providers in Chile must be registered with and authorised by the Financial Market Commission or the Central Bank of Chile, depending on the products offered.

Advertisers must also meet applicable local legal requirements and obtain Google certification. The revised policy creates an opportunity for eligible brokers to advertise these products through Google in both markets. Google said violations would trigger a warning at least seven days before any account suspension.

Kalshi Targets Broker Distribution

Kalshi is seeking to expand access to its event contracts through brokerage platforms, with liquidity central to its pitch to financial services firms. In an interview with Finance Magnates, Andy Ross, the exchange’s Head of Institutional, said connecting brokers to an existing venue allows them to access a shared order book rather than build their own exchange and clearing infrastructure.

Kalshi has already launched an API-based service with Apex Fintech Solutions, allowing brokers to integrate its contracts into their platforms. Tastytrade was the first broker to go live. Ross said firms onboarding to or already trading on Kalshi collectively manage more than $1 trillion in assets.

The exchange is also preparing to launch perpetual futures linked to foreign exchange markets and offers market data to firms that do not trade its contracts directly.

Plus500 Agrees to Acquire Brazilian Broker Guru

Plus500 has conditionally agreed to acquire full ownership of Guru Corretora de Títulos e Valores Mobiliários Ltd, a regulated Brazilian broker-dealer.

The London-listed group said the transaction would be funded from its existing cash resources, which exceeded $860 million.

The acquisition gives Plus500 access to local licences from Brazil’s Securities and Exchange Commission and Central Bank of Brazil. These authorisations would allow it to expand its domestic offering to Brazilian shares, futures, options and fixed-income securities.

Chief Executive David Zruia said the deal provides the licences, local team and regulatory framework needed to operate in the market. The agreement follows Plus500’s acquisition of US broker-dealer Hedge, which is intended to support its planned US multi-asset platform.

Brokers Face Pressure as CPA Rates Outpace Initial Deposits

Customer acquisition costs are putting pressure on forex and CFD brokers as cost-per-acquisition payments increasingly exceed clients’ initial deposits. Anish Lal, Chief Business Development Officer at BlackBull Markets, noted that brokers may pay $800 to acquire a client who makes an initial deposit of $400 to $500.

They must then rely on further deposits and trading activity over the following six to 12 months to recover the expense. If the client leaves after one or two months, the acquisition becomes loss-making.

Dubai Compliance Chiefs Earn Up to $425K as Cyprus FX Salaries Rise 14%

FinTop Consulting’s 2026 salary surveys showed substantial differences in compensation across Dubai, London and Cyprus. Dubai-based Chief Compliance Officers can earn between $310,000 and $425,000 annually, with the lower benchmark matching the upper salary benchmark for Chief Technology Officers.

London Heads of Compliance can earn up to $251,000, while regulatory specialists handling additional responsibilities command premiums of 10% to 20%.

Cyprus recorded annual salary growth of 14% across its foreign exchange and fintech sectors, compared with approximately 4% across UAE financial services. The figures point to differing compensation trends across the three financial centres.

Dubai’s compliance salaries also exceed those available for several commercial executive roles, although some technology and risk positions can command higher maximum pay.

IG Applies for UK Gambling Licence to Offer Prediction Markets

IG Group has applied for a UK gambling licence to offer prediction markets covering sports, politics and entertainment, with a launch planned for early 2027.

The application was submitted through its London subsidiary, IG View Limited, which appears on the Gambling Commission’s register under the trading name ig prediction markets.

The application remains pending, and the licence has not been granted.

The company also plans to introduce financial event contracts for UK professional clients in the fourth quarter of 2026. Its expansion follows an agreement to acquire US fantasy sports and prediction markets operator Underdog for up to approximately $1.3 billion.

The deal is expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027. IG’s plans would extend its offering beyond conventional leveraged trading products.

Capital.com UAE Clients Trade $1 Trillion

Capital.com clients in the United Arab Emirates traded $1.06 trillion during the first half of 2026, accounting for more than two-fifths of the broker’s $2.45 trillion in total trading volume.

UAE trading volume increased 27.7% from the second half of 2025, while closed trades rose 48% to 80.9 million, according to the broker’s H1 2026 Pulse Report.

However, only 18.3% of UAE trades had a stop-loss set, the lowest proportion among seven markets covered. Germany recorded the highest rate at 34.1%, followed by the Netherlands at 32.8%.

Across Capital.com, 22.4% of closed trades carried a stop-loss set at entry. The report also found that positions closed after a stop-loss trigger recorded 39% lower average losses, although it described this as a correlation rather than proof of causation.

Hantec Trader Rebrands as RZR Funded

Hantec Trader, the proprietary trading business within the Hantec Group, has rebranded as RZR Funded and changed the name of its operating company from Hantec Trader Limited to RZR Funded Limited. The firm said the change establishes a separate identity for its prop trading operations as it prepares for further development.

The business remains part of the Hantec Group and continues to be powered by Hantec Markets Mauritius, the group’s retail broker arm regulated by the Financial Services Commission.

RZR Funded Director Bashaar Gokal said the company was expanding its executive team and preparing to introduce new asset classes and trading tools. He added that existing traders should not expect immediate operational changes as a result of the rebrand.

Google Reopens CFD Advertising in Denmark and Chile

Google has updated its policy on complex speculative financial products to permit advertising for CFDs, rolling spot forex and similar products in Denmark and Chile. The changes take effect in October, although Google has not specified an exact date.

Advertisers in Denmark must hold the relevant authorisation from the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority, while providers in Chile must be registered with and authorised by the Financial Market Commission or the Central Bank of Chile, depending on the products offered.

Advertisers must also meet applicable local legal requirements and obtain Google certification. The revised policy creates an opportunity for eligible brokers to advertise these products through Google in both markets. Google said violations would trigger a warning at least seven days before any account suspension.

Kalshi Targets Broker Distribution

Kalshi is seeking to expand access to its event contracts through brokerage platforms, with liquidity central to its pitch to financial services firms. In an interview with Finance Magnates, Andy Ross, the exchange’s Head of Institutional, said connecting brokers to an existing venue allows them to access a shared order book rather than build their own exchange and clearing infrastructure.

Kalshi has already launched an API-based service with Apex Fintech Solutions, allowing brokers to integrate its contracts into their platforms. Tastytrade was the first broker to go live. Ross said firms onboarding to or already trading on Kalshi collectively manage more than $1 trillion in assets.

The exchange is also preparing to launch perpetual futures linked to foreign exchange markets and offers market data to firms that do not trade its contracts directly.

Plus500 Agrees to Acquire Brazilian Broker Guru

Plus500 has conditionally agreed to acquire full ownership of Guru Corretora de Títulos e Valores Mobiliários Ltd, a regulated Brazilian broker-dealer.

The London-listed group said the transaction would be funded from its existing cash resources, which exceeded $860 million.

The acquisition gives Plus500 access to local licences from Brazil’s Securities and Exchange Commission and Central Bank of Brazil. These authorisations would allow it to expand its domestic offering to Brazilian shares, futures, options and fixed-income securities.

Chief Executive David Zruia said the deal provides the licences, local team and regulatory framework needed to operate in the market. The agreement follows Plus500’s acquisition of US broker-dealer Hedge, which is intended to support its planned US multi-asset platform.

title: Wells Fargo and five others object to OKX-ICE tokenized stock listings: Report
summary: As of Friday, 22 companies had filed objections as part of the joint venture’s proposed tokenized stock platform under the SEC’s innovation exemption.
content:
As of Friday, 22 companies had filed objections as part of the joint venture’s proposed tokenized stock platform under the SEC’s innovation exemption.

Six more companies have reportedly filed objections to having their stocks listed in tokenized form on the proposed platform as part of a joint venture between cryptocurrency exchange OKX and the New York Stock Exchange’s parent company, the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).

According to a Friday Reuters report, the proposed stock platform, called OKXICE, had 22 companies total objecting to having their US stock listings tokenized. Among the most recent objections reportedly included Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and Intuit, adding their names to Microsoft and Google’s parent company Alphabet in the last week.

Notably, 16 of the companies were listed on Nasdaq, while only six of the stocks were available on the NYSE. Nasdaq released guidance for companies considering the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) innovation exemption for trading tokenized stocks in September, noting issuers “must be cautious about their participation,” saying “consequences for liquidity, price discovery, and long-term shareholder value may not become apparent until well after the experiment is underway.”

Speaking to Cointelegraph on Tuesday, OKXICE co-chair and former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo said that company expected there to be more objections in an effort to avoid being the first ones testing the stock model. The venture proposed 62 companies listing tokenized stocks when it filed with the SEC earlier this month.

Cointelegraph reached out to Intuit for comment on the company’s decision to opt-out of the initiative, but did not receive an immediate response. Spokespeople for Wells Fargo and Arm Holdings declined to comment.

title: NY Seeks $1.37 Billion Judgment Against Operators of NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Scheme
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

NY Seeks $1.37 Billion Judgment Against Operators of NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Scheme
Two successive crypto frauds took investors for more than $1.1 billion. Now New York's attorney general is asking a court to make the operators pay it back—with interest.
This post NY Seeks $1.37 Bill...
content:
New York Attorney General Letitia James is trying to secure a $1.37 billion judgment against the operators of NovaTech and its predecessor AWS Mining, two successive cryptocurrency investment schemes that allegedly defrauded hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide out of more than $1 billion.

Alleged founders Cynthia and Eddy Petion never appeared in court and, according to the AG’s office, fled the country.

“NovaTech and AWS Mining scammed thousands of vulnerable New Yorkers by telling them they were making a safe investment when in reality, they were victims of a pyramid scheme,” James said in a statement. “These scammers targeted immigrant and religious communities with the promise of a better life but instead robbed them of their life savings.”

The schemes, AWS Mining and later NovaTech, relied on promoters who recruited heavily in Haitian and other immigrant communities — through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats, and ads in Haitian Creole.

AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts promising 15 to 20 percent monthly returns and 200 percent within 15 months. It collapsed in 2019. The Petions then launched NovaTech, marketed as a registered hedge fund broker, promising weekly trading returns of two to four percent — more than 140 percent a year.

Those returns were fabricated, according to prosecutors. Records from B2Broker, which supplied NovaTech’s white-label trading platform, show that of the more than $1 billion investors deposited between 2019 and 2023, only about $26 million was ever actually traded — and NovaTech’s traders lost $18.2 million of that. Returns to earlier investors came from newer deposits, not trading. When NovaTech collapsed in mid-2023, tens of thousands of investors could not withdraw their funds.

The AG is also seeking $134.5 million the Petions allegedly withdrew to their own wallets from the investor account Cynthia Petion solely controlled, plus $4.7 million tied to the earlier AWS Mining scheme. A default judgment entered in August 2025 already bars the couple and their companies from the securities, commodities, and cryptocurrency industries.

Separately, four of the scheme’s top promoters have agreed to pay nearly $6 million in disgorgement to victims and accepted the same industry bans.

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Blockstream Launches Institutional Consulting Services, Opens Lugano Office
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Blockstream Launches Institutional Consulting Services, Opens Lugano Office
Blockstream will offer its engineering expertise to banks and asset managers from a new Swiss base.
This post Blockstream Launches Institutional Consulting Services, Opens Lugano Office first appeared on Bi...
content:
Blockstream has launched a consulting business for financial institutions and opened an office in Lugano, Switzerland, the company shared today. The expansion gives banks, asset managers and other institutions direct access to the firm’s engineering teams and Bitcoin infrastructure, Blockstream said. 

Blockstream Consulting Services will support institutions through the evaluation, design and implementation of Bitcoin-based financial infrastructure. The company said the business will develop solutions for tokenized asset issuance, confidential settlement and related infrastructure, with services spanning technical strategy, system architecture, integration and implementation.

From Lugano, Blockstream plans to serve clients across Switzerland, including Zurich, Geneva and Zug. The company said the office will serve as a hub for its European operations, supporting client relationships, strategic partnerships and collaboration with the region’s financial and technology communities.

“Switzerland is an important market for Blockstream given its longstanding banking tradition and supportive regulatory framework for digital assets,” said Peter Bain, chief marketing officer of the company. “We look to provide regional expertise in markets where we see demand for Bitcoin infrastructure. Our consulting business, combined with our new office in Lugano, will bring tailored Bitcoin solutions to financial institutions across Europe.”

Founded in 2014, Blockstream develops technology and services across Bitcoin custody, settlement, payments, asset issuance and self-custody. Its products include the Liquid Network sidechain, Elements, Simplicity, Core Lightning, the Jade hardware wallet and the Blockstream App. This year, the company launched Simplicity smart contracts on Liquid and added Lightning support to Jade.

Bitcoin adoption by financial institutions

The company said the consulting business draws on that experience, with capabilities in cryptography, protocol engineering, security and financial technology. Multidisciplinary teams will give institutions access to the firm’s technical staff from initial evaluation through deployment.

“The next phase of Bitcoin adoption is its integration into existing financial systems,” said Adam Back, Blockstream’s co-founder and CEO. “Our extensive experience in Bitcoin cryptography, protocol development and engineering gives Blockstream the technical expertise to address the complexities of integrating Bitcoin into traditional financial infrastructure.”

The company framed the move as part of a long-term commitment to Switzerland and a broader strategy of building a presence in key markets to support institutional Bitcoin adoption. 

The country has become a center for digital asset firms, with Zug’s “Crypto Valley” and a regulatory framework that permits banks to hold and trade bitcoin on behalf of clients.

There was no pricing disclosed, headcount for the Lugano office or named clients for the consulting business. The company said the Lugano office is open and that consulting engagements are available to institutions across Europe.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: IRS plans lower tax disclosure penalties, including for crypto: Forbes
summary: The US tax agency is targeting faster resolutions and more flexible payment options for taxpayers voluntarily disclosing past tax violations under a planned program overhaul.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedOct 23, 2026

The US tax agency is targeting faster resolutions and more flexible payment options for taxpayers voluntarily disclosing past tax violations under a planned program overhaul.

The US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) is preparing to overhaul its voluntary disclosure program, with plans to reduce penalties and accelerate the resolution of tax violations, including those involving cryptocurrencies, according to a Friday report by Forbes.

IRS Criminal Investigation Chief Jarod Koopman said the agency aims to introduce the revised program before December, with a target of resolving cases within 120 days of taxpayers completing the required submission process.

The overhaul would reportedly not establish a separate disclosure process for digital assets. Koopman told attendees at the UCLA Extension Tax Controversy Conference that the IRS would handle digital assets through the same voluntary disclosure procedures used for other forms of tax noncompliance.

The IRS official also indicated that penalties under the revised program would be substantially lower than those currently imposed, although he did not provide specific figures. The agency is considering allowing taxpayers to settle outstanding liabilities through installment plans or offers in compromise.

The proposed changes would mark a shift from the existing process, which can take a year or longer to complete, according to Forbes. The IRS’s current voluntary disclosure program is intended for taxpayers whose willful failure to comply with tax laws could expose them to criminal prosecution, rather than those who made unintentional reporting errors.

Meanwhile, lawmakers are considering a separate voluntary disclosure program aimed at crypto taxpayers, including those who made unintentional reporting errors. Section 502 of the proposed Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act would establish a process for correcting past violations with defined penalties, unlike the IRS’s existing program, which primarily addresses willful tax noncompliance. The bill cleared the House Ways and Means Committee in September.

title: Initia halts blockchain after exploit reportedly drains over $2.6M
summary: The blockchain suspended its layer-1 network and rollups after security researchers identified unauthorized token minting and millions in assets transferred to Ethereum.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedOct 23, 2026

The blockchain suspended its layer-1 network and rollups after security researchers identified unauthorized token minting and millions in assets transferred to Ethereum.

Initia halted its layer-1 blockchain and rollups after blockchain sleuths reported an exploit that allowed an attacker to mint tokens without authorization and drain more than $2.6 million in crypto assets.

The network was halted at 3:41 p.m. UTC on Friday following a security incident, Initia said in a post on X. The team said it was working with security researchers, validators and exchanges to determine the full extent of the impact.

Blockchain security researcher Spreek first flagged the exploit on Friday, reporting that an attacker had minted tokens without authorization and converted approximately $2.6 million into other assets, with additional funds still being moved.

DeFi platform D2 Finance later reported that the attacker exploited a vulnerability to mint 2 million AUSD tokens without sufficient backing. The attacker then used cross-chain transfers to withdraw approximately 1.4 million AUSD, 105 Ether (ETH) and 1.08 million USDC (USDC) to Ethereum.

The stolen assets were subsequently consolidated into an Ethereum wallet holding approximately 1,135.5 ETH, worth $2.73 million, according to D2 Finance. The firm attributed the exploit to a vulnerability in a Move function that allowed the attacker to create unbacked tokens and exchange them for assets on Ethereum.

Source: Initia

Initia is a layer-1 blockchain designed to support a network of interconnected rollups, known as Minitias. Its native token, INIT, briefly fell to around $0.115 on Friday before rebounding above $0.15, according to CoinGecko data. The token was trading near $0.1496 at the time of writing, an increase of about 14% over the previous 24 hours.

Initia has not publicly confirmed the estimated losses or the precise cause of the exploit, and the extent of the impact on users and the timeline for restoring network operations remain unclear. Cointelegraph was unable to contact Initia for additional comment through its official X account.

title: US senator probes Tether after reported deal with ex-Trump crypto adviser
summary: The Democratic ranking member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations asked Paolo Ardoino for records related to a reported deal between Tether and Nxum.
content:
Update (Oct. 23, 6:27 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include a response from Tether.

Senator Richard Blumenthal has requested information from Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino after a Wall Street Journal report said that the stablecoin issuer had inked a $6.3 million deal with a marketing company co-founded by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines.

In a Thursday letter to Ardoino, the Connecticut lawmaker said that the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations demanded “records and information related to contracts, payments, communications, and lobbying” between Tether and Nxum, Hines’ company. The probe into Nxum, Tether and Hines, according to Blumental, was part of what the senator called the Trump administration’s “self-enrichment and self-dealings with cryptocurrency firms.”

“While Hines failed to divest his one-third stake in Nxum [...] he worked closely over encrypted messaging applications with Nxum to coordinate lobbying, advocacy, and browbeating of members of Congress that were opposed to, or had sought changes to, pending stablecoin legislation,” said Blumenthal. “Those messages also reportedly demonstrate that Tether was directly coordinating Nxum’s lobbying efforts on the GENIUS Act which would regulate stablecoins, with CEO Paolo Ardoino demanding that Nxum ‘obliterate’ the legislation’s opponents.”

The lawmaker added:

“The highly unusual terms and nature of Tether’s business relationship with both Nxum and Bo Hines raise alarming ethical and legal concerns, indicating that Tether was likely well aware of the illegality and impropriety of issuing payments to a current White House official with such a direct role in shaping cryptocurrency legislation that was instrumental to its business.”

Hines worked as executive director as President’s Council of Advisers on Digital Assets from January to August 2025, when he left the White House to join Tether as a “strategic adviser.” He later became CEO of Tether US. Harry Jung, another crypto adviser in the Trump administration, left his position in July 2026 and joined Nxum as a managing director in August.

A Tether spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the company was aware of the allegations and an external counsel ”found no evidence of wrongdoing” after a previous ”in-depth internal investigation into the matter.”

Related: Trump didn‘t mention ‘crypto’ once in White House cybercrime roundtable

Trump, his family and members of his administration continue to face scrutiny over accusations that they are reaping financial windfalls from crypto policies on laws over which they have control or influence. The president disclosed earning $1.4 billion from investments related to crypto in 2025.

Crypto ties could be a factor in midterm elections

While Blumenthal has limited authority as the Democratic ranking member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, the results of the 2026 midterm elections could potentially change party control in the House of Representatives and Senate. This could give the Connecticut lawmaker and other Democratic additional authority to conduct investigations into Trump and his administration’s ties to the crypto industry, including those which could present conflicts of interest.

As of Friday, event contracts on prediction market platforms Kalshi and Polymarket favored Democrats retaking majority control of both chambers of Congress in 2027, with 92% and 68% chances on Kalshi for the House and Senate, respectively. US Election Day is on Nov. 3.

title: Bitcoin Core Ends Long Embargoes for Bugs AI Can Rediscover
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Core Ends Long Embargoes for Bugs AI Can Rediscover
Bitcoin Core now fast-tracks fixes and disclosures for vulnerabilities that AI can easily rediscover, ending the long embargoes those bugs once received.
This post Bitcoin Core Ends Long Embargoes for Bugs AI Can Rediscove...
content:
Bitcoin Core has changed its security disclosure policy to speed up fixes for vulnerabilities that large language models can find with little effort, ending the months-long embargoes those bugs once received.

Maintainers merged the change to the project’s security policy on Thursday. Chaincode Labs developer Antoine Poinsot, who wrote the proposal, announced it in a message to the Bitcoin Development Mailing List the same day.

“We recently experienced an increase in the number of reports for security vulnerabilities that can be easily (re-)discovered,” Poinsot wrote. “This is largely due to LLMs drastically reducing the bar to find certain classes of issues or identify covert fixes.”

How the policy worked before

Bitcoin Core, the software that runs on most nodes in the Bitcoin network, has graded each reported vulnerability by severity and timed its disclosure to match. Low-severity flaws were made public two weeks after the next major version shipped. 

Medium- and high-severity issues stayed under embargo until two weeks after the last affected release reached end of life, a span that could stretch to a year.

The extended timelines gave node operators, many of whom upgrade at a slow pace, time to move to patched software before details became public. In practice, the approach meant fixes went unreleased for older maintained versions and arrived with the next major release.

Poinsot argued that this tradeoff fails for bugs that are easy to rediscover. “The embargo period achieves little but it delays the availability of a fixed release,” the policy reads.

What changes

During triage, Bitcoin Core can flag a vulnerability as “easily discoverable,” a category the policy defines as issues that can be found “with minimal effort, such as through a simple LLM prompt.” The label is open to flaws found by other means as well.

For those issues, the project will backport a fix to every maintained major version, cut point releases as soon as possible and publish a security advisory with some details at the same time as the fixed software. 

Poinsot acknowledged that such fixes will have less testing time before they reach users.

Vulnerabilities outside that category keep the existing severity-based schedule. Critical bugs, those that could enable coin theft at the protocol level, inflate the supply or cause a permanent chain split, remain outside the standard policy and will be handled case by case.

Developer Antoine Riard pushed for an option to ship a fix without an advisory and withhold details on a case-by-case basis. Poinsot declined, writing that alerting users without details “could create more risk unnecessarily” by prompting a rushed migration among users who would otherwise be unaffected.

A summer of AI-driven reports

The change follows months of heightened pressure on Bitcoin’s open-source projects. In late July, a volunteer group of 16 developers known as the Bitcoin Red Team ran AI models across 390 bitcoin repositories in about a day and logged 4,962 findings, including 85 rated critical.

Within days, a BTCPay Server flaw the group had reported in private was exploited on live merchant servers, draining Lightning nodes.

In August, Core Lightning developers told operators to upgrade or disconnect after AI-generated reports to the project proved accurate.

The Red Team effort followed a Coldcard hardware wallet exploit in which attackers drained 594 BTC in 25 minutes on July 30. Losses across four sweeps approached $114 million.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose Over $635M In One Day Following Oil Price Spike
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin ETFs Lose Over $635M In One Day Following Oil Price Spike 
Investors this week were buying bitcoin ETFs but that all changed on Thursday. 
This post Bitcoin ETFs Lose Over $635M In One Day Following Oil Price Spike  first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathe...
content:
U.S. investors quickly reversed course on Thursday, cashing out over half a billion dollars from spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds as risk-off sentiment surfaced again. 

A total of $635.6 million left the funds on Thursday, data from Farside Investors shows. The redemptions put downward pressure on the price of bitcoin, which dropped under $81,000 at one point. 

The coin has since rebounded and was recently trading for nearly $81,669, down just 1% over a 24-hour period. 

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust saw the biggest outflows, with investors cashing out over $254 million. Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund followed, losing close to $218 million. 

Over $109 million left the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF; Morgan Stanley’s fund and Bitwise’s ETF lost nearly $30 million and over $27 million, respectively. 

But the investment vehicles this week have this week received net positive investment of over $439 million. 

Investors went into “risk-off” mode after flare ups in the Middle East sent the price of oil higher. Brent crude hit its highest price in five months after Yemeni rebel group the Houthis on Thursday attacked Saudi Arabia, sparking concerns over more disruption to energy supplies. 

Bitcoin’s price has been rattled this year since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran, halting oil supplies as ships have struggled to pass through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, where a fifth of the world’s oil passes through. 

A higher oil price can hurt the price of bitcoin and other “risk-on” assets because it increases the chances of the U.S. central bank raising interest rates. 

Bitcoin has typically done well in a low interest rate environment because it means the asset has more liquidity to rally. 

Investors on Thursday also sold off tech stocks, which had rallied earlier in the week off the back of SpaceX’s impressive earnings. 

Analysts are saying bitcoin is entering a bull market again. Data last month showed that  the leading cryptocurrency crossed above its 365-day moving average — a typical sign it is out of a bear market — following a strong run in August. 

Bitcoin notched a record of $126,080 in October 2025 but then began to sink later that month after the biggest liquidation event in crypto history saw over $19 billion in bets closed. 

The coin spent the first half of 2026 trading well below that level but picked up again in August and September, having its best quarter in years. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: OpenAI Cuts $150 Billion Valuation as Anthropic Reports $80 Billion Loss: Is the AI Boom Cracking?
summary: OpenAI has reportedly lowered its proposed valuation by $150 billion to $1.25 trillion, while rival Anthropic’s draft IPO prospectus reveals an $80.7 billion first-half net loss, highlighting the financial pressures behind the artificial intelligence boom.
content:
Skip to content

OpenAI has reportedly lowered its proposed valuation by $150 billion to $1.25 trillion, while rival Anthropic’s draft IPO prospectus reveals an $80.7 billion first-half net loss, highlighting the financial pressures behind the artificial intelligence boom.

The developments come as investors scrutinize infrastructure spending, rising computing costs, and the path to profitability. Although both OpenAI and Anthropic continue to attract substantial investor interest, their latest financial disclosures raise questions about whether AI revenue can justify the enormous cost of developing and operating advanced models.

Key Takeaways

  • OpenAI lowered its proposed valuation from $1.4 trillion to $1.25 trillion while seeking approximately $30 billion in fresh funding.
  • Anthropic reported $16.3 billion in first-half 2026 revenue and an $80.7 billion net loss, according to its draft IPO prospectus.
  • Approximately $72 billion of Anthropic’s reported loss came from non-cash accounting adjustments linked to convertible financial instruments.
  • Rising computing expenses, long-term infrastructure commitments, and uncertain returns are increasing scrutiny of AI companies ahead of potential public listings.

OpenAI Valuation Drops $150 Billion: Is the AI Boom in Trouble?

OpenAI has reduced its proposed valuation to $1.25 trillion from $1.4 trillion as negotiations progress on a funding round of approximately $30 billion, according to Bloomberg reporting published on October 23, 2026. The $150 billion adjustment represents a reduction of about 10.7% from its previous target.

OpenAI lowered its valuation target by $150 billion to $1.25 trillion for a proposed $30 billion funding round, with negotiations ongoing. Source: Rohan Paul via X

The revised figure remains well above OpenAI’s March 2026 post-money valuation of $852 billion, established after a reported $122 billion funding round. The new target is approximately 47% higher, indicating that the company’s fundraising ambitions remain substantial despite the adjustment.

The revision does not mean OpenAI has lost $150 billion in realized market value. It reflects a change in the valuation proposed during private fundraising negotiations, which remain ongoing.

The timing is significant. Technology stocks have faced selling pressure following mixed earnings from companies including Meta Platforms and Tesla, intensifying investor concerns that AI infrastructure spending could be growing faster than the returns it generates.

Developing advanced AI systems requires substantial investment in specialized chips, data centers, electricity, and computing capacity. Investors are increasingly assessing whether commercial revenue can grow quickly enough to cover these expenses and support the valuations attached to AI developers.

Why Is OpenAI’s Valuation Falling?

OpenAI’s revised target follows reported investor resistance to its earlier $1.4 trillion valuation, according to the Financial Times. The adjustment may help narrow the gap between the company’s fundraising expectations and investors’ willingness to commit additional capital.

The broader technology selloff has added pressure, as investors reassess the financial returns expected from AI-related investments. However, the available information does not establish that infrastructure spending concerns alone caused OpenAI’s valuation adjustment.

The distinction between a proposed valuation and a completed funding valuation is important. Private-company valuations depend on negotiated financing terms and expectations about future growth, rather than daily market prices. Until the round closes, OpenAI’s $1.25 trillion target remains subject to change.

OpenAI Seeks $30 Billion Ahead of Potential IPO

OpenAI continues to pursue approximately $30 billion in new funding to finance its expansion. Bloomberg reported that Coatue Management was discussing a role as a co-lead investor, while BlackRock and investment funds from the United Arab Emirates were also involved in fundraising discussions.

Bloomberg reports OpenAI has lowered its target valuation to $1.25 trillion for a $30 billion funding round amid investor pushback, down from an initial $1.4 trillion. Source: @business via X

Investor commitments could be finalized by the end of the following week, although the final funding amount and valuation remained uncertain.

The negotiations come as OpenAI prepares for a potential initial public offering in 2027. A public listing would bring greater scrutiny of its financial performance, capital requirements, and progress toward sustainable profitability.

The company faces a balancing act: continuing to invest in model development and computing capacity while demonstrating that its products can generate enough recurring revenue to support those costs. Its reported spending projections of approximately $278 billion in cash through 2030 illustrate the scale of that challenge.

OpenAI’s fundraising outcome could also influence investor expectations for Anthropic, which is preparing for its own potential IPO. Both companies must convince prospective investors that rapid growth can eventually translate into sustainable financial returns.

Anthropic S-1 Shows Red-Hot Growth, Risks, and Massive Computing Costs

Anthropic’s draft IPO prospectus offers another perspective on the financial pressures facing AI developers. According to The Wall Street Journal’s review of the document, the company generated $16.3 billion in revenue during the first half of 2026, up from $1.1 billion in the same period a year earlier.

Anthropic’s draft IPO filing reports $16.3 billion in H1 2026 revenue and an $80.7 billion net loss, largely driven by $72 billion in non-cash valuation charges on convertible instruments. Source: @WSJ via X

Despite that expansion, Anthropic recorded an $80.7 billion net loss, compared with $13 billion a year earlier. Approximately $72 billion of the latest loss came from non-cash accounting charges associated with changes in the estimated value of convertible financial instruments that could become company shares.

Those adjustments do not represent equivalent cash outflows from daily operations. Investors must therefore distinguish the reported net loss from operating expenses and cash-flow performance when assessing Anthropic’s financial health.

Infrastructure costs provide a clearer view of the resources required to operate its business. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, compared with $2.3 billion a year earlier. The six-month total also exceeded its reported infrastructure spending for all of 2025.

Long-term commitments create additional financial exposure. Reports based on the draft prospectus place Anthropic’s cloud, computing, and infrastructure obligations above $600 billion, with some estimates reaching $750 billion when prospective agreements are included. Much of the spending is tied to contracts that cannot easily be cancelled.

These commitments help secure the capacity needed to meet demand, but they also reduce flexibility if revenue growth slows or computing requirements change.

Growth That Most Companies Never See

Anthropic’s revenue expansion remains substantial. First-half revenue rose from $1.1 billion in 2025 to $16.3 billion in 2026, reflecting growing demand for its AI products and services.

Its Claude Code coding assistant has helped attract developers and enterprise customers seeking tools to support software development and automate technical tasks. This business-focused approach can generate recurring revenue when customers incorporate AI products into their regular workflows.

Anthropic’s third-quarter revenue reportedly increased 45% to $16.8 billion from $11.6 billion in the second quarter. Although the increase remains significant, the sequential growth rate was slower than the more-than-doubling reported between the first and second quarters.

That moderation matters because investors must assess whether revenue can continue expanding fast enough to support rising infrastructure costs. Even a rapidly growing business can face financial pressure if expenses increase at a comparable or faster rate.

Investors have reportedly discussed an Anthropic valuation near $1.5 trillion, below earlier expectations of approximately $2 trillion. The proposed figure would still represent a substantial valuation, placing considerable weight on the company’s ability to maintain growth and improve margins.

The Bill for Being Compute-Starved

Access to computing capacity is a central constraint for advanced AI developers. Training models and operating them at scale require specialized chips, data centers, electricity, and cloud services. Securing sufficient capacity is essential, but competition for those resources can make expansion expensive.

Anthropic’s reported infrastructure commitments reflect the challenge. While estimates of its total obligations vary, the draft prospectus and related reporting point to hundreds of billions of dollars in potential spending over the coming years.

Non-cancellable agreements can provide greater certainty about access to computing resources, but they also create fixed obligations. If demand weakens, Anthropic may be unable to reduce those costs quickly enough to protect its margins.

Its relationships with infrastructure providers add another complication. Amazon, Google, and Microsoft supply cloud services while also developing their own AI products. This overlap creates competing commercial interests and may affect the availability, pricing, and terms of computing agreements.

Anthropic must therefore secure the resources required to serve customers without allowing infrastructure costs to outpace the revenue those resources generate.

Why the Whole Sector Is Watching

Anthropic’s potential IPO could test investor appetite for AI companies that combine rapid revenue growth with significant infrastructure commitments. Its financial disclosures give prospective investors a clearer view of both the commercial opportunity and the costs associated with competing in the sector.

The reception could influence expectations for OpenAI and other AI developers considering public listings. Investors will be watching whether strong revenue growth can support the valuations companies seek, particularly as infrastructure spending absorbs increasing amounts of capital.

OpenAI’s projected cash spending of approximately $278 billion through 2030 underscores the investment required to develop and operate advanced AI systems. The figure also highlights why investors are paying closer attention to capital allocation and the timing of future returns.

Broader technology-market volatility adds uncertainty. If investors become less willing to fund expensive expansion plans, AI companies could face pressure to lower their valuation expectations, reduce spending, or demonstrate a clearer path to profitability.

Is the AI Boom Cracking?

OpenAI’s valuation adjustment and Anthropic’s reported $80.7 billion first-half loss do not establish that the AI boom is ending. OpenAI’s proposed valuation remains above its previous funding benchmark, while Anthropic’s revenue growth demonstrates substantial commercial demand for AI products.

The developments instead highlight a shift in investor priorities. Alongside growth and technical progress, investors increasingly want evidence that AI revenue can cover computing expenses, long-term infrastructure obligations, and the continuing cost of developing advanced models.

OpenAI must secure funding on terms that support its expansion, while Anthropic faces scrutiny of its operating economics and infrastructure commitments ahead of a potential IPO. Both companies will need to show that their business models can support their substantial capital requirements.

The next phase of the AI market may depend less on the amount of capital companies attract and more on how effectively they convert that investment into sustainable earnings and cash flow. The latest disclosures point to greater financial scrutiny, but whether that develops into a broader market correction will depend on actual performance, investor demand, and the industry’s ability to deliver lasting returns.

title: Franklin Templeton Clears Final Hurdle For ETFs That Turn Stock Dividends Into Bitcoin
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Franklin Templeton Clears Final Hurdle For ETFs That Turn Stock Dividends Into Bitcoin
Franklin Templeton, the $1.7 trillion asset manager, registered two Nasdaq-listed funds yesterday. Both launch with a 95/5 split between U.S. stocks and bitcoin, and every dividend buys more bitc...
content:
Franklin Templeton has taken the last regulatory step before launching two exchange-traded funds that convert stock dividends into bitcoin. 

On October 22, Franklin Templeton filed a Form 8-A with the Securities and Exchange Commission to register shares of the Franklin US Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF and the Franklin US Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF for trading on the Nasdaq. A prospectus filed the same day lists an effective date of October 27.

The filings for both funds arrived in June without tickers or fees. Four months later, the details are in.

How the funds work

The Equity fund, ticker FBEQ, tracks the VettaFi US Large-Cap 500 Bitcoin DRIP Index. The index holds the 500 largest U.S. companies by market capitalization, weighted by float-adjusted market cap. 

As of September 30, it held 499 stocks ranging from $10.2 billion to $5.5 trillion in size, with a concentration in information technology.

At inception, the index allocates 95% to those stocks and 5% to bitcoin. Each dividend the companies pay, regular or special, is reinvested into bitcoin at the market open on the day after the ex-date. The bitcoin share of the portfolio grows with each payment.

A traditional dividend reinvestment plan, or DRIP, buys more shares of the company that paid the dividend. Franklin’s version routes that cash into bitcoin. 

For a holder, the dividend stream from the largest companies in America becomes a recurring bitcoin purchase, with no exchange account, no wallet and no custody decisions.

The bitcoin position has limits. At each quarterly rebalance, an allocation above 5% is trimmed to 4.5%. If bitcoin exceeds 20% of the index between rebalances, it is cut back to 4.5% within two business days, and the proceeds return to stocks. The result is a stock fund with a bitcoin sleeve, not a bitcoin fund.

The ETF does not hold bitcoin on-chain. It gains exposure through bitcoin exchange-traded products, including Franklin’s own spot fund, through bitcoin futures and options, or through depositary receipts, in some cases via a Cayman Islands subsidiary.

FBEQ carries a 0.09% expense ratio with no 12b-1 fee. Franklin Advisory Services manages the fund, with Franklin Templeton Institutional as sub-advisor. Dina Ting, Hailey Harris, Joe Diederich and Basit Amin serve as portfolio managers.

The Innovation fund follows the same mechanic on the VettaFi US Innovation 100 Bitcoin DRIP Index, which draws from the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq.

A deeper bet on bitcoin

Franklin Templeton filed for a spot bitcoin ETF in September 2023 and launched it as EZBC in January 2024. In April, the firm acquired 250 Digital and formed Franklin Crypto, an institutional digital asset division. Franklin Templeton CEO Jenny Johnson has argued that blockchains threaten Wall Street’s fee structure more than its technology.

The DRIP funds extend that strategy to investors who may never buy bitcoin on their own. A retiree holding an S&P 500-style fund in a brokerage account can, through FBEQ, let dividends from the companies she already owns build a bitcoin position over years.

The prospectus warns that investors can lose money, and that bitcoin’s price swings may affect the fund’s net asset value. Whether that trade-off appeals to the audience Franklin Templeton is targeting will become clear after October 27.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: 25 BLOOM Participants Join 3 Asian Central Banks to Advance Cross-Border Digital Money
summary:
Key Takeaways: Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand are working together on cross-border settlement with digital money. Banks and technology companies join large crypto and payments companies like Ripple, Circle, Coinbase, and
The post 25 BLOOM Participants Join 3 Asian Central Banks to Advance Cross-B...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand are working together on cross-border settlement with digital money.
  • Banks and technology companies join large crypto and payments companies like Ripple, Circle, Coinbase, and Visa for BLOOM.
  • The project addresses three issues: multi-jurisdictional settlement, interoperability of networks, and programmable compliance protocols.

Three central banks from the Southeast Asian region are sharing efforts to work together on digital money, and both traditional finance and the crypto industry are joining forces to enhance cross-border transactions. Singapore’s Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) announced on October 23 that Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Bank of Thailand (BOT) had joined its BLOOM initiative as policymaker members.

  • Three Central Banks Coordinate Digital Money Rules
  • Ripple, Circle and Coinbase Join a Growing Network
    • Three Priorities for Cross-Border Settlement
    • Lower Costs Could Support Institutional Crypto Adoption

Three Central Banks Coordinate Digital Money Rules

BLOOM is Borderless, Liquid, Open, Online and Multi-currency. The public-private effort aims to align thinking by regulators, financial institutions, payment networks, and technology providers about interborder digital money.

The project covers different forms of digital money, including tokenized bank deposits and regulated stablecoins. BLOOM is looking to make alternative arrangements, agree and work together and continue to respect the specific regulatory requirements for each jurisdiction.

This also applies to crypto markets, as fiat can fuel digital transfers and settlement, but this has to be followed with acceptance by counterparties, compatibility with infrastructure and adherence to local rules and laws.

The partnership also will serve to coordinate international standards and supervisory expectations, providing financial institutions with a more uniform approach to cross-border transactions, MAS said.

Read More: DBS and Citi Enable 24/7 USD Payments With Tokenized Deposits, Cutting Settlement to Minutes

Ripple, Circle and Coinbase Join a Growing Network

The new BLOOM members are Airwallex, Mastercard, Maybank, Monee, Nium, Ripple, ShopeePay, Visa and World Bank Group.

It brings on the existing participants including Circle, Coinbase, Anchorage Digital, DBS, J.P. Morgan, Standard Chartered, Stripe, Temasek, and other financial and tech companies. Hence, the project collects institutions that have experience in stablecoins, crypto infrastructure, banking, and international payments.

Three Priorities for Cross-Border Settlement

Within the course of this BLOOM participants will concentrate on the following three areas. They will look at how institutions can embrace diverse forms of digital money and complete transactions between their counterparties in different markets.

Second, they will be engaged in interoperability efforts, tackling the essential technical and operational challenges between the different payments systems and digital currencies. The third is the investigation of programmable controls, such as which can be installed in digital money transactions to verify identity, conduct sanctions screening, and ensure that the transactions are safe.

The issue with the faster digital transfers is not enough because these are vital for regulated stablecoins and tokenized deposits, as would the ability to accept, exchange and settle funds compliantly across jurisdictions.

Lower Costs Could Support Institutional Crypto Adoption

Common implementation frameworks and aligned commercial arrangements could streamline the need for financial institutions to have to negotiate individual processes with each counterparty or market, MAS said. That has the potential to reduce implementation costs and make new services available sooner.

World Bank Group involvement also adds a development viewpoint, such as through the introduction of modern payment mechanisms, cross-border payments, and greater access to finance.

title: Reflect Lets Anyone Launch a Solana Stablecoin in Under a Minute With Shared Yield
summary:
Key Takeaways: Reflect has released the Create tool, which enables the user to mint stablecoins with a brand on Solana in one go. Creators have discretion over the collateral accepted
The post Reflect Lets Anyone Launch a Solana Stablecoin in Under a Minute With Shared Yield appeared first on Crypto...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Reflect has released the Create tool, which enables the user to mint stablecoins with a brand on Solana in one go.
  • Creators have discretion over the collateral accepted and the allocation of underlying yields to the creators and token holders.
  • Solana claims that the launch process takes less than a minute.

Reflect has launched a new Solana-based tool that turns stablecoin creation into a near-instant process. The product, named Create, allows users to select collateral, incorporate their own branding, decide a yield-sharing plan, and create a stablecoin in a single transaction on a blockchain.

Create is live. Launch a stablecoin with your name on it, on @Solana, in one transaction.

Choose the collateral from a reviewed set and decide how the interest splits between you and your holders. Press build and the coin exists.

https://t.co/lwQ3rf33lJ https://t.co/MuqcgsrLJW

— Reflect (@reflectmoney) October 22, 2026

  • Reflect Turns Stablecoin Creation Into a One-Transaction Process
  • Creators Can Split Yield With Token Holders
    • Collateral Selection Determines How the Stablecoin Works

Reflect Turns Stablecoin Creation Into a One-Transaction Process

Reflect announced the launch of a new Create service on Solana, providing faster launch for businesses and developers of their own customizable stablecoins. Rather than developing token launch from scratch, users adopt any of the reviewed collaterals and set up the distribution plan for the gained revenue.

Finally, when it has been configured, it is built and the stablecoin is deployed to the Solana network. Solana’s Twitter account also added to the launch, stating that users would be able to secure their own stable coin within less than a minute.

Launch your own stablecoin on Solana in under a minute

— Solana (@solana) October 22, 2026

The product’s main focus is the emerging market of crypto companies, including their infrastructure, who desire a branded digital dollar without having to implement a reserve management system, token mechanics, and yield logic on their own.

Read More: Tesla’s $TSLA Stock Token Lands on Solana Across 10+ Apps via Backpack Securities

Creators Can Split Yield With Token Holders

The model of reflect, which is stablecoin, associates each stablecoin with yield-generating collateral. The creator determines the size of that return and whether it comes back to the holders or is kept by the issuer or application.

That makes it easy for any fintech, payment platform, marketplace, payroll provider, or crypto products to provide users with a brandable dollar asset while still earning a profit.

For example, a creator could direct most of the underlying yield to token holders while keeping a smaller portion as platform income. The following day’s return may vary due to the return produced by the cash held as collateral for the stablecoin.

Collateral Selection Determines How the Stablecoin Works

Reflect does not allow the creators to have any assets they want. Collateral should be sourced from a reviewed set that is assessed based on liquidity, asset quality and technical risk, according to the company.

Eligible assets must also be transferable and compatible with the user, meaning that there cannot be restrictions on their use onchain in any way. This means Create is not simply a token generator. The structure of the stablecoin is directly linked with assets behind the coins.

Additionally, liquidity in the venues underlying the redemption mechanism matters, and reserves might not be provisioned as readily during periods of market mayhem.

With its most recent addition, Create is further developing stablecoin infrastructure on the Solana payments and tokenization ecosystem.

title: Bank of Korea Wants Stablecoins Written Into Forex Law as Crypto Bill and Tax Fight Come to a Head
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bank of Korea Wants Stablecoins Written Into Forex Law as Crypto Bill and Tax Fight Come to a Head
The Bank of Korea told lawmakers it will draft a forex law amendment this year to regulate stablecoins as a means of payment, a plan that points to tighter cross-border controls rathe...
content:
The Bank of Korea plans to draft an amendment to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act with the government before year-end that would regulate stablecoins as a means of payment, according to a written submission to the National Assembly’s annual audit reported by Korean outlet Digital Asset.

The central bank’s October 22 report, a follow-up to last year’s audit, says it is consulting with the government on measures to regulate cross-border transactions in virtual assets. 

While building a monitoring system based on foreign exchange network reporting, the bank said, it plans to prepare the amendment with the government this year to regulate stablecoins as a means of payment, among other aims.

That is a plan to write a bill, not a bill in itself. There is no draft text, no named token and no passage date. And “means of payment” is a defined term in Korean forex law: an instrument whose cross-border movement must be reported. 

On that reading, the amendment would put dollar stablecoins under the same controls as a wire to New York, not make them legal tender at a Seoul convenience store.

The BOK pointed to settlement outside the banking system, mixers and regulatory gaps around personal wallets as factors that ease illegal transactions. Bitcoin holders who self-custody in Korea should take note: the country’s capital controls are the reason the kimchi premium exists, and a tighter forex net around crypto would entrench those controls rather than ease them.

The forex work runs in parallel with the Digital Asset Basic Act, the licensing and stablecoin-issuance framework flagged alongside spot bitcoin ETF approval in the government’s 2026 growth strategy. 

Financial Services Commission chairman Lee Eog-weon told lawmakers Thursday that consultations are in their final stage and the bill will follow as soon as possible, Bloomingbit reported. 

The BOK said it will work with ministries to limit transactions that exploit the gap until that law exists.

South Korea’s crypto tax discussions

The gap has a date attached. Korea’s crypto income tax is due to take effect January 1, 2027, according to The Block, after three postponements, and lawmakers have questioned taxing a market before the law defining it is passed. 

Lee said Thursday the tax should “take various circumstances into full consideration,” per Yonhap. Democratic Party leader Kim Min-seok called Thursday for a “thorough final review,” a shift from a party that had insisted on 2027. 

Two petitions, one to repeal the tax and one to defer it two years, each cleared the 50,000 signatures that force a legislative review. 

The National Tax Service has not moved: it plans to finalize its draft tax notice by October 30, Digital Asset reported.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.
